rules.name: 代码格式规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
该规则旨在确保代码的可读性，特别是在紧凑的单行声明之间增加空行，改善代码格式。

## 规则意义
在紧凑的代码结构中，缺少空行会降低代码的可读性。通过在单行声明之间添加空行，可以有效提升代码的可读性和维护性，帮助开发者更容易地理解代码逻辑和结构。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
object P1 { get; }
object P2 { get; }
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
object P1 { get; }

object P2 { get; }
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule aims to ensure code readability by adding a blank line between single-line declarations to improve code formatting.

## Rule Meaning
In dense code structures, the lack of blank lines can reduce readability. By adding blank lines between single-line declarations, we can effectively enhance code readability and maintainability, making it easier for developers to understand the code logic and structure.

## Error Example
'''csharp
object P1 { get; }
object P2 { get; }
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
object P1 { get; }

object P2 { get; }
'''
rules.description: 此规则建议在单行声明之间添加空行，以提高代码的可读性和整洁性。
rules.description_en: This rule suggests adding a blank line between single-line declarations to improve code readability and neatness.

rules.name: 单行声明间的空行添加
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在不同类型的单行声明之间添加空行，以提高代码的可读性和组织性。

## 规则意义
代码的可读性对于维护和开发至关重要。通过在不同类型的单行声明之间添加空行，可以更清晰地分隔代码逻辑，减少理解困难。

## 错误示例
```csharp
object P { get; }
object this[int index] { get; }
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
object P { get; }

object this[int index] { get; }
```


## Correct Example

rules.name: 属性列表换行规整
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议将C#代码中的属性列表放置在单独的行上，以提高代码的可读性和一致性。

## 规则意义
将属性列表放在单独的行上可以使代码更加清晰，特别是在有多个属性或注解时，有助于提高代码的可读性和可维护性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
enum Foo
{
    A,
    [Obsolete] B,
    C,
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
enum Foo
{
    A,
    [Obsolete]
    B,
    C,
}
```
rules.content_en:

## Error Example
```csharp

{
    A,
    [Obsolete] B,
    C,
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
enum Foo
{
    A,
    [Obsolete]
    B,
    C,
}
```
rules.description: 建议将属性列表放置在单独的行上以提高代码的可读性和一致性。
rules.description_en: Suggests placing attribute lists on their own line to improve readability and consistency of the code.

rules.name: 代码块大括号格式
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则确保代码块的大括号格式化为单独一行或多行。这种格式提升代码的可读性和维护性，符合代码格式的最佳实践。

## 规则意义
采用一致的大括号格式使代码更易于阅读和理解，特别是在代码审查和团队协作中。统一的代码风格也能减少开发人员之间的矛盾，提高代码的整体质量。

## 错误示例
```csharp
void Foo() { Bar(); }
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
void Foo()
{
    Bar();
}
```

## Correct Example

```csharp
    Bar();
}
```

rules.name: 二元操作符换行规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议在二元操作符前或后换行，以提高代码可读性和一致性。

## 规则意义
在二元操作符处换行可以提高代码的可读性，使操作符及其操作数更易于辨识。这样做有助于避免误解操作符的优先级，并确保代码风格的一致性。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
if (x &&
    y &&
    z)
{
}
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
if (x
    && y
    && z)
{
}
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule recommends placing a newline before or after binary operators to improve code readability and consistency.

## Rule Meaning
Placing new lines at binary operators enhances readability and makes operators and their operands more distinguishable. This helps avoid misunderstandings of operator precedence and ensures consistent code style.

## Error Example
'''csharp
if (x &&
    y &&
    z)
{
}
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
if (x
    && y
    && z)
{
}
'''
rules.description: 此规则建议在二元操作符前后进行换行，以提高代码的可读性和一致性。
rules.description_en: This rule recommends placing new lines before or after binary operators to improve code readability and consistency.

rules.name: 三元运算符换行规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
该规则建议在使用三元运算符时，在'? :'运算符之前或之后插入换行符，以提高代码的可读性和一致性。

## 规则意义
遵循此规则可以帮助开发者统一代码风格，使代码更易于维护和理解。特别是在条件表达式较长时，新的行结构可以显著提高可读性。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
var y = x ?
    Foo() :
    Bar();
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
var y = x
    ? Foo()
    : Bar();
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule suggests adding a newline before or after the '?:' operator when using the ternary operator to improve code readability and consistency.

## Rule Meaning
Following this rule helps developers maintain a consistent code style, making the code easier to maintain and understand. This is particularly beneficial when the condition expression is lengthy, as a new line structure significantly improves readability.

## Error Example
'''csharp
var y = x ?
    Foo() :
    Bar();
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
var y = x
    ? Foo()
    : Bar();
'''
rules.description: 此规则建议在使用三元运算符时，在'? :'运算符之前或之后插入换行符，以提高代码的可读性和一致性。
rules.description_en: This rule suggests adding a newline before or after the '?:' operator when using the ternary operator to improve code readability and consistency.

```csharp
if (x) Foo();
```

## 正确示例

```csharp
if (x)
```

rules.description: 此规则确保在条件语句中，嵌入的代码需要放在独立的一行，以提高代码的整洁度和可读性。
rules.description_en: This rule ensures that in conditional expressions, the embedded code should be placed on its own line to enhance the tidiness and readability of the code.

rules.name: 枚举成员行格式
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议在定义枚举类型时，每个枚举成员应放在单独一行，以提高代码的可读性和维护性。

## 规则意义
枚举成员放在同一行可能会导致代码可读性差，难以找到和修改特定的枚举成员。在团队开发中，保持代码格式统一有助于提升代码质量和协作效率。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
enum Foo { A, B, C, }
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
enum Foo
{
    A,
    B,
    C,
}
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule suggests that, when defining an enum type, each enum member should be placed on its own line to improve code readability and maintainability.

## Rule Meaning
Putting enum members on the same line can reduce code readability, making it difficult to find and modify specific enum members. Maintaining a consistent code style in team development helps enhance code quality and collaboration efficiency.

## Error Example
'''csharp
enum Foo { A, B, C, }
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
enum Foo
{
    A,
    B,
    C,
}
'''
rules.description: 此规则建议在定义枚举类型时，每个枚举成员应放在单独一行，以提高代码的可读性和维护性。

rules.name: 代码行规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
当相邻的多个语句写在同一行时，应将每个语句拆分为独立的行，以提高代码的可读性和维护性。

## 规则意义
此规则有助于提高代码的可读性，避免多个语句挤在一行，从而降低代码理解的难度。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
Foo(); Bar();
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
Foo();
Bar();
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
When multiple adjacent statements are written on the same line, each statement should be split into separate lines to enhance the readability and maintainability of the code.

## Rule Meaning
This rule helps improve code readability by avoiding multiple statements crammed into a single line, thus reducing the difficulty of understanding code.

## Error Example
'''csharp
Foo(); Bar();
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
Foo();
Bar();
'''
rules.description: 将多个语句放在同一行上会降低代码的可读性。建议将每个语句放在单独的行上。
rules.description_en: Placing multiple statements on the same line reduces code readability. It is recommended to put each statement on a separate line.

rules.name: 类型参数约束换行规范
rules.content:

rules.description: 此规则要求 C# 代码中的类型参数约束放在单独的行上，以提高可读性。

rules.description: 删除同类单行声明之间的空行，以提高代码可读性。

rules.name: 使用换行符作为新行
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议使用换行符 (Linefeed) 作为文本中的新行符号，而不是其他字符组合，例如回车换行符 (Carriage Return + Linefeed)。

## 规则意义
统一使用换行符有助于保持代码风格一致性，并提高跨平台文本处理的兼容性。在大多数现代操作系统中，换行符是默认的新行符号。

## 错误示例
```csharp
string text = "Hello, World!\r\nThis is another line.";
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
string text = "Hello, World!\nThis is another line.";
```

rules.name: 代码行长度规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
本规则用于检查代码行的长度是否超过了设定的最大长度限制。默认的最大长度为140个字符。

## 规则意义
限制代码行长度有助于提高代码可读性，使其在各种编辑器或查看器中更易于查看和维护。超长的代码行可能会导致阅读困难，特别是在代码审查或版本控制比较时。

## 错误示例
```csharp
// 行长度超过140个字符
var example = "这是一条超长的字符串，它的长度已经超过了设定的限制，使得这行代码难以阅读和维护。";
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
// 将字符串分为多行，遵守长度限制
var example = "这是一条比较长的字符串，" +
               "但通过分隔符将其分为多行。";
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule checks if the line of code exceeds the specified maximum length limit. The default maximum length is 140 characters.

## Rule Meaning
Restricting the line length helps improve code readability and makes it easier to view and maintain in various editors or viewers. Overly long lines of code may cause difficulty in reading, especially during code reviews or version control comparisons.

## Error Example
```csharp
// Line length exceeds 140 characters
var example = "This is a long string that exceeds the set limit, making it difficult to read and maintain.";
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
// Breaking the string into multiple lines, adhering to length limits
var example = "This is a rather long string, " +
               "but it is split into multiple lines.";
```
rules.description: 确保代码行的长度不超过设定的最大字符数限制，以提高代码可读性。

rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#的 `switch` 语句中， `default` 标签应始终放在最后。此规则帮助确保代码的可读性和逻辑清晰性。

## 规则意义
规范 `switch` 结构有助于增强代码的可维护性，同时避免潜在的逻辑错误。当 `default` 标签位于 `switch` 语句的最后时，代码执行顺序更符合直觉和习惯。

## 错误示例
```csharp
switch (s)
{
    default:
    case "a":
    case "b":
        break;
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
switch (s)
{
    case "b":
    case "a":
    default:
        break;
}
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In C#'s `switch` statements, the `default` label should always be placed last. This rule helps ensure code readability and logical clarity.

## Rule Meaning
Structuring `switch` statements properly enhances code maintainability and avoids potential logical errors. When the `default` label is placed last, the execution order of the code is more intuitive and consistent with expectations.

## Error Example
```csharp
switch (s)
{
    default:
    case "a":
    case "b":
        break;
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
switch (s)
{
    case "b":
    case "a":
    default:
        break;
}
```

# Rule Overview
This rule suggests combining consecutive `Enumerable.Where` method calls to improve code readability and execution efficiency.

## Rule Meaning
Combining `Enumerable.Where` method chains can reduce unnecessary iterations, optimize performance, and makes the logic clearer and more concise.

## Error Example
'''csharp
IEnumerable<string> x = items.Where(f => Foo(f)).Where(f => Bar(f));
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
IEnumerable<string> x = items.Where(f => Foo(f) && Bar(f));
'''
rules.description: 该规则建议合并连续的`Where`方法调用，以优化代码性能和可读性。

rules.content:


rules.name: 局部变量常量化
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议将未修改的局部变量标记为`const`，从而提高代码的可读性和稳定性。

## 规则意义
标记为`const`的变量值在编译时确定，能提高代码的稳定性，避免无意中的修改并且可能带来性能优化。

## 错误示例
```csharp
string s = "a";
string s2 = s + "b";
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
const string s = "a";
string s2 = s + "b";
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule suggests marking local variables as `const` if they are never modified, to improve code readability and stability.

## Rule Meaning
Variables marked as `const` have their values determined at compile time, which can improve code stability, prevent unintentional modifications, and may offer performance optimizations.

## Error Example
```csharp
string s = "a";
string s2 = s + "b";
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
const string s = "a";
string s2 = s + "b";
```
rules.description: 此规则建议对于未被修改的局部变量，应将其标记为`const`，以提高代码的安全性和可读性。
rules.description_en: This rule suggests that local variables which are not modified should be marked as `const` to enhance code safety and readability.

rules.name: 枚举类型按位操作的使用须加Flags属性
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在没有应用[Flags]属性的枚举类型上进行按位运算可能导致不可预期的结果。

## 规则意义
此规则旨在确保对枚举类型进行按位操作时，枚举类型被正确标记为[Flags]。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
dayOfWeek x = dayOfWeek | DayOfWeek.Tuesday;
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
[Flags]
enum DayOfWeek
{
    None = 0,
    Sunday = 1,
    Monday = 2,
    Tuesday = 4,
    // 其他星期的定义
}

DayOfWeek x = DayOfWeek.Monday | DayOfWeek.Tuesday;
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Performing bitwise operations on enum types without the [Flags] attribute may lead to unexpected results.

## Rule Meaning
This rule ensures that enum types with bitwise operations are properly marked with the [Flags] attribute.

## Error Example
'''csharp
dayOfWeek x = dayOfWeek | DayOfWeek.Tuesday;
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
[Flags]
enum DayOfWeek
{
    None = 0,
    Sunday = 1,
    Monday = 2,
    Tuesday = 4,
    // Other days definitions
}

DayOfWeek x = DayOfWeek.Monday | DayOfWeek.Tuesday;
'''
rules.description: 该规则用于识别在未标记为Flags的枚举类型上执行按位操作的情况。
rules.description_en: This rule identifies bitwise operations on enum types that are not marked with the Flags attribute.

rules.content:
# 规则概述
当枚举类型具有 `FlagsAttribute` 时，应声明一个具有零值的枚举成员。这是一个最佳实践，因为零值成员通常用于表示“无选项”或“未设置”。

## 规则意义
在使用标识属性时，定义一个零值枚举成员可以提供更清晰的代码表示，确保枚举在默认状态下更易于理解和控制。

## 错误示例
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    A = 1,
    B = 2
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    None = 0,
    A = 1,
    B = 2
}
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
When an enum type has the `FlagsAttribute`, an enum member with a zero value should be declared. This is a best practice because the zero value member is typically used to represent 'no options' or 'unset'.

## Rule Meaning
Defining a zero-value enum member when using the Flags attribute allows for clearer code representation and ensures that enums are more understandable and controllable in their default state.

## Error Example
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    A = 1,
    B = 2
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    None = 0,
    A = 1,
    B = 2
}
```
rules.description: 当枚举声明`FlagsAttribute`时，应该定义一个具有零值的成员，以表示“未设置”或“无选项”。
rules.description_en: When an enum is declared with `FlagsAttribute`, a member with a zero value should be defined to represent 'unset' or 'no options'.

rules.name: 枚举成员排序规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#代码中，建议将枚举（enum）的成员按其值进行排序，从而提高代码的可读性和维护性。

## 规则意义
将枚举成员排序有助于提高代码的可读性，方便开发者快速理解枚举成员的排列规则。此外，有序的枚举成员可以帮助在版本控制中更容易追踪变化和减少合并冲突。

## 错误示例
```csharp
public enum Foo
{
    D = 4,
    B = 2,
    A = 1,
    C = 3
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
public enum Foo
{
    A = 1,
    B = 2,
    C = 3,
    D = 4
}
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In C# code, it is recommended to sort the members of an enum based on their values to improve code readability and maintainability.

## Rule Meaning
Sorting enum members enhances code readability and allows developers to quickly understand the arrangement of enum members. Furthermore, well-ordered enum members can facilitate tracking changes in version control and reduce merge conflicts.

## Error Example
```csharp
public enum Foo
{
    D = 4,
    B = 2,
    A = 1,
    C = 3
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
public enum Foo
{
    A = 1,
    B = 2,
    C = 3,
    D = 4
}
```
rules.description: 此规则建议将枚举成员按值进行排序，以提升代码的可读性和维护性。
rules.description_en: This rule suggests sorting enum members by their values to enhance code readability and maintainability.

rules.name: 复合枚举值包含未定义标志
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在定义[Flags]类型的枚举时，应该只包含已定义的枚举值。此规则用于检测复合枚举值是否包含未定义的枚举标志。

## 规则意义
确保枚举值组合的正确性，以避免运行时错误和逻辑缺陷，提高代码的健壮性和可维护性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    None = 0,
    A = 1,
    B = 2,
    C = 4,
    D = 8,
    X = 17  // X 包含未定义的标志
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    None = 0,
    A = 1,
    B = 2,
    C = 4,
    D = 8,
    X = A | D  // X 包含已定义的标志
}
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
When defining an enum with [Flags] attribute, it should only include defined enum values. This rule checks whether the composite enum value contains any undefined flags.

## Rule Meaning
Ensures the correctness of enum value combinations, prevents runtime errors and logical defects, and enhances code robustness and maintainability.

## Error Example
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    None = 0,
    A = 1,
    B = 2,
    C = 4,
    D = 8,
    X = 17  // X contains undefined flags
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    None = 0,
    A = 1,
    B = 2,
    C = 4,
    D = 8,
    X = A | D  // X contains defined flags
}
```
rules.description: 检测复合枚举值中是否包含未定义的标志，以提高代码的正确性和稳定性。
rules.description_en: Checks for undefined flags within composite enum values to enhance code correctness and stability.

rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议在定义枚举类型时，为每个枚举成员显式指定整数值。显式声明枚举值可以提高代码的可读性和维护性，并避免潜在的错误。

## 规则意义
通过为枚举成员显式指定值，可以确保每个枚举成员的值是明确的且稳定的。这有助于在版本更新或重构时减少错误风险，并且对于希望对枚举成员进行版本控制的场景尤其重要。

## 错误示例
```csharp
public enum Foo
{
    A,
    B,
    C,
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
public enum Foo
{
    A = 0,
    B = 1,
    C = 2,
}
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule advises explicitly assigning integer values to each member of an enum type. Explicitly declaring enum values improves code readability and maintainability and prevents potential errors.

## Rule Meaning
By explicitly assigning values to enum members, you can ensure that each enum member has a clear and stable value. This helps reduce error risks during version updates or refactoring and is particularly important in scenarios where version control of enum members is desired.

## Error Example
```csharp
public enum Foo
{
    A,
    B,
    C,
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
public enum Foo
{
    A = 0,
    B = 1,
    C = 2,
}
```
rules.description: 枚举类型应显式声明每个成员的值，以提高代码的可读性和稳定性。
rules.description_en: Enum types should explicitly declare the value of each member to improve code readability and stability.

rules.name: 避免连续赋值操作
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在代码中，避免多个变量通过链式赋值进行赋值操作。这会降低代码的可读性，增加理解成本，容易导致错误。

## 规则意义
链式赋值容易掩盖错误的赋值顺序或遗漏赋值，也使代码的意图不够清晰。因此，应避免在同一行中多个变量连环赋值，用分开的行来确保代码清晰和可靠。

## 错误示例
```csharp
x = y = z;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
y = z;
x = y;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Avoid using chained assignments where multiple variables are assigned a value in a single statement. This decreases code readability and can lead to errors.

## Rule Meaning
Chained assignments can obscure assignment order errors or missing assignments and can make the code less clear. It is better to assign each variable separately to ensure the code is clear and reliable.

## Error Example
```csharp
x = y = z;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
y = z;
x = y;
```

rules.content:

在C#中，如果一个属性只在构造函数中被赋值，而不需要在类的其他部分修改，那么将其改为只读属性可以提高代码的安全性和可维护性。

rules.content_en:

```csharp
public object Foo { get; private set; }
```

```csharp
public object Foo { get; }
```

rules.content:

rules.content_en:

rules.description: 当类继承的基类已经实现某接口时，在派生类中不应再次声明实现该接口。

rules.name: 使用常量代替字段
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议在可能的情况下使用 `const` 常量来代替 `readonly` 字段。这可以提高代码的性能，因为常量在编译时确定，而 `readonly` 字段在运行时分配。

## 规则意义
使用常量可以使代码更为高效，并减少内存占用。当一个值在生命周期内没有改变时，应尽量使用 `const`。

## 错误示例
```csharp
private static readonly int _foo = 0;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
private const int _foo = 0;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule suggests using `const` constants instead of `readonly` fields where possible. This can improve the performance of the code since constants are determined at compile time while `readonly` fields are assigned at runtime.

## Rule Meaning
Using constants can make the code more efficient and reduce memory usage. When a value does not change over its lifecycle, `const` should be used whenever possible.

## Error Example
```csharp
private static readonly int _foo = 0;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
private const int _foo = 0;
```
rules.description: 此规则建议在可能的情况下使用常量代替字段，以提高代码性能并减少内存占用。
rules.description_en: This rule suggests using constants instead of fields where possible to improve code performance and reduce memory usage.

rules.name: 移除冗余的自动属性初始化
rules.content:
# 规则概述
本规则建议开发者移除自动属性中不必要的默认值初始化，以提高代码的可读性和简洁性。

## 规则意义
在C#中，自动属性的默认值通常是其类型的默认值（例如，引用类型为`null`），显式设置为默认值是多余的。因此，移除这些冗余的初始化可以使代码更简洁，减少不必要的重复。

## 错误示例

public string Foo { get; set; } = null;
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
public string Foo { get; set; }
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule suggests developers remove unnecessary default value initializations in auto-properties to improve code readability and conciseness.

## Rule Meaning
In C#, auto-properties typically have default values that are the same as their type's default (e.g., `null` for reference types). Explicitly setting them to these default values is redundant. Therefore, removing such redundant initializations can make the code cleaner and reduce unnecessary repetition.

## Error Example
'''csharp
public string Foo { get; set; } = null;
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
public string Foo { get; set; }
'''
rules.description: 该规则建议移除自动属性的冗余初始化以简化代码。
rules.description_en: This rule suggests removing redundant initializations in auto-properties to simplify the code.

rules.name: 字符串拼接优化
rules.content:

string s = "a" + "b";

string s = "ab";

rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule suggests merging multiple string literals into a single string literal to improve code readability and performance.

string s = "a" + "b";

rules.description: 建议将多个字符串字面量的拼接改为单个字符串字面量。

rules.name: 枚举值命名组合
rules.content:
# 规则概述
该规则建议在定义标有 [Flags] 特性的枚举值时，将组合的枚举值表示为其基本枚举值的按位组合，而不是使用数字常量。

## 规则意义
使用枚举值的组合名称可以提高代码的可读性和可维护性，使得代码更容易理解和更少出错。如果枚举值中已经存在常量组合值，那么就应该使用其名称组合。

## 错误示例
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    None = 0,
    A = 1,
    B = 2,
    C = 4,
    ABC = 7  // 此处的 "7" 应替换为 "A | B | C"
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    None = 0,
    A = 1,
    B = 2,
    C = 4,
    ABC = A | B | C
}
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule recommends that when defining enum values marked with the [Flags] attribute, combined enum values should be represented as a bitwise combination of their basic enum values instead of numerical constants.

## Rule Meaning
Using the combination names of enum values enhances the readability and maintainability of the code, making it easier to understand and less prone to errors. If constant combination values are already present in the enum, their names should be used for combinations.

## Error Example
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    None = 0,
    A = 1,
    B = 2,
    C = 4,
    ABC = 7  // The "7" here should be replaced with "A | B | C"
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
[Flags]
public enum Foo
{
    None = 0,
    A = 1,
    B = 2,
    C = 4,
    ABC = A | B | C
}
```
rules.description: 该规则建议为标有 [Flags] 特性的枚举值使用组合名称而不是数值常量来声明，从而提高代码的可读性与可维护性。
rules.description_en: This rule recommends using combination names instead of numeric constants for enum values marked with the [Flags] attribute to enhance code readability and maintainability.

rules.name: 不必要的逐字字符串字面量使用
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#中，逐字字符串字面量（以`@`符号开头的字符串）通常用于需要包含转义字符（如换行、制表符等）的场合。然而，当字符串不包含任何需要转义的字符时，使用逐字字符串字面量是多余的。

## 规则意义
移除不必要的逐字字符串字面量可以使代码更加简洁明了，提高代码可读性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
string s = @"textWithoutEscapeSequence";
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
string s = "textWithoutEscapeSequence";
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In C#, verbatim string literals (strings prefixed with `@`) are typically used when the string needs to contain escape characters (such as newlines or tabs). However, when the string does not contain any characters that require escaping, using a verbatim string literal is unnecessary.

## Rule Meaning
Removing unnecessary verbatim string literals can make the code clearer and improve readability.

## Error Example
```csharp
string s = @"textWithoutEscapeSequence";
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
string s = "textWithoutEscapeSequence";
```
rules.description: 检测并移除不包含需转义字符时不必要的逐字字符串字面量。
rules.description_en: Detect and remove unnecessary usage of verbatim string literals when no escaping characters are present.

```csharp
var x = Enumerable.Select(items, f => f.ToString());
```

rules.name: 使用ThenBy代替重复OrderBy
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议在对同一集合进行多次排序时，使用`ThenBy`来代替重复的`OrderBy`调用。`OrderBy`用于首次排序，后续的排序条件应使用`ThenBy`。

## 规则意义
使用`ThenBy`代替多次`OrderBy`可以提高代码的可读性，并减少性能开销，因为`ThenBy`不会重新对集合进行完整排序，而是在已有排序的基础上再进行。

## 错误示例
```csharp
var x = items.OrderBy(f => f.Surname).OrderBy(f => f.Name);
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
var x = items.OrderBy(f => f.Surname).ThenBy(f => f.Name);
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule suggests using `ThenBy` instead of repeated `OrderBy` calls when sorting the same collection multiple times. `OrderBy` is used for the first sort, while subsequent sort conditions should use `ThenBy`.

## Rule Meaning
Using `ThenBy` instead of multiple `OrderBy` calls improves code readability and reduces performance overhead, as `ThenBy` performs additional sorting based on the existing sort.

## Error Example
```csharp
var x = items.OrderBy(f => f.Surname).OrderBy(f => f.Name);
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
var x = items.OrderBy(f => f.Surname).ThenBy(f => f.Name);
```
rules.description: 建议重复排序时使用`ThenBy`而非多次使用`OrderBy`。
rules.description_en: Suggest using `ThenBy` instead of multiple `OrderBy` calls when sorting repeatedly.

rules.name: 使用方法链

rules.name: 避免空引用异常
rules.content:
# 规则概述
本规则旨在帮助开发者在代码中避免出现空引用异常（NullReferenceException），这种异常会导致程序崩溃并影响用户体验。

## 规则意义
空引用异常是C#开发中常见的错误之一，当试图访问的对象为null时，就会出现这种异常。通过此规则，我们可以提前发现潜在问题，并进行必要的空检查，提升代码的健壮性和稳定性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
string s = items.FirstOrDefault().ToString();
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
string s = items.FirstOrDefault()?.ToString();
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule aims to help developers avoid NullReferenceExceptions in their code, which can cause the program to crash and adversely affect the user experience.

## Rule Meaning
NullReferenceException is a common error in C# development that occurs when attempting to access an object that is null. By applying this rule, we can detect potential issues in advance and perform necessary null checks, improving the robustness and stability of the code.

## Error Example
```csharp
string s = items.FirstOrDefault().ToString();
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
string s = items.FirstOrDefault()?.ToString();
```
rules.description: 该规则通过识别可能产生空引用异常的代码，指导开发人员在必要情况下进行空检查。
rules.description_en: This rule identifies code that may produce NullReferenceExceptions and guides developers to perform null checks when necessary.

public class FooAttribute : Attribute
{
}
'''

}
'''

rules.description_en: The AttributeUsageAttribute should be used in custom attribute classes to specify its usage targets and constraints.

'''

rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议在定义泛型类或方法时，类型参数的约束应按照声明顺序排列。

在代码中统一类型参数约束的顺序有助于提高代码的可读性和一致性。尽管编译器不会因为这种不一致性报错，但对团队开发来说，保持代码风格的统一非常重要。

rules.name: 使用短路运算符
rules.content:
# 规则概述
通过短路运算符`&&`和`||`替换非短路运算符`&`和`|`来提高代码执行效率。

## 规则意义
短路运算符能够在第一操作数确定结果的情况下避免第二操作数的执行，提高代码效率及性能。当你在布尔表达式中用`&`和`|`代替`&&`和`||`时，可能会导致不必要的执行。因此，推荐使用短路运算符。

## 错误示例
```csharp
bool result = boolExpr1 & boolExpr2;
bool result2 = boolExpr1 | boolExpr2;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
bool result = boolExpr1 && boolExpr2;
bool result2 = boolExpr1 || boolExpr2;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Replace non-short-circuit operators `&` and `|` with short-circuit operators `&&` and `||` to improve code execution efficiency.

## Rule Meaning
Short-circuit operators can avoid the execution of the second operand if the result is determined by the first operand, enhancing code efficiency and performance. Using `&` and `|` in boolean expressions instead of `&&` and `||` may lead to unnecessary execution. Therefore, it is recommended to use short-circuit operators.

## Error Example
```csharp
bool result = boolExpr1 & boolExpr2;
bool result2 = boolExpr1 | boolExpr2;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
bool result = boolExpr1 && boolExpr2;
bool result2 = boolExpr1 || boolExpr2;
```
rules.description: 使用短路运算符可以提高代码的效率和性能,在布尔表达式中建议使用`&&`和`||`代替`&`和`|`。
rules.description_en: Using short-circuit operators can improve the efficiency and performance of the code. It is recommended to use `&&` and `||` instead of `&` and `|` in boolean expressions.

# 规则概述
空容忍运算符在一些情况下可以帮助避免空引用异常，但如果在代码中不需要它，则会导致不必要的代码复杂性。

## 规则意义

rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
The null-forgiving operator can help prevent null reference exceptions in some cases, but if not needed, it adds unnecessary complexity to the code.

## Rule Meaning
Using unnecessary null-forgiving operators increases code reading difficulty and may be misleading. Adhering to a concise and clear code style helps improve code maintainability.

'''

# 规则概述
此规则用于检查 `[DiagnosticAnalyzer]` 的属性中是否使用了未知或错误的语言名称。

## 规则意义
确保使用的语言名称是有效的，以防止运行时错误和分析器无法正确被应用到适当的语言。

## 错误示例
```csharp
[DiagnosticAnalyzer("C")]
class FooDiagnosticAnalyzer : DiagnosticAnalyzer
{
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
[DiagnosticAnalyzer("C#")]
class FooDiagnosticAnalyzer : DiagnosticAnalyzer
{
}
```
rules.content_en:

## Rule Meaning
Ensuring the language name is valid prevents runtime errors and ensures the analyzer is correctly applied to the appropriate language.

## Error Example
```csharp
[DiagnosticAnalyzer("C")]
class FooDiagnosticAnalyzer : DiagnosticAnalyzer
{
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
[DiagnosticAnalyzer("C#")]
class FooDiagnosticAnalyzer : DiagnosticAnalyzer
{
}
```

rules.name: 导出代码重构提供程序名称规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
导出代码重构提供程序时，应指定`ExportCodeRefactoringProviderAttribute`的`Name`属性，以确保该提供程序在多个提供程序中能够被明显区分。

## 规则意义
未指定`Name`可能会导致在使用多个重构提供程序时辨识度差，增加代码管理和维护的难度。

## 错误示例
```csharp
[ExportCodeRefactoringProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp)]
class FooCodeRefactoringProvider : CodeRefactoringProvider
{
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
[ExportCodeRefactoringProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(FooCodeRefactoringProvider))]
class FooCodeRefactoringProvider : CodeRefactoringProvider
{
}
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
When exporting a code refactoring provider, it's recommended to specify the `Name` property of the `ExportCodeRefactoringProviderAttribute` to distinguish the provider among multiple ones.

## Rule Meaning
Omitting the `Name` can lead to low recognition among multiple refactoring providers, complicating code management and maintenance.

## Error Example
```csharp
[ExportCodeRefactoringProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp)]
class FooCodeRefactoringProvider : CodeRefactoringProvider
{
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
[ExportCodeRefactoringProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(FooCodeRefactoringProvider))]
class FooCodeRefactoringProvider : CodeRefactoringProvider
{
}
```
rules.description: 确保在导出代码重构提供程序时，指定名称属性以提高识别度。
rules.description_en: Ensure that the name property is specified when exporting a code refactoring provider to enhance recognizability.

rules.name: XML文档注释校验禁用
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则要求每个项目配置都包含XML文档文件作为编译输出的一部分。如果项目配置禁用XML文档注释的校验，将导致文档注释语义未被检查，可能会导致错误增加。

## 规则意义
未启用XML文档文件输出可能导致忽略关于XML文档注释的潜在问题，从而影响代码质量和文档一致性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
// 项目文件中未设置生成XML文档文件
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net5.0</TargetFramework>
    <!-- 没有GenerateDocumentationFile设置 -->
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
// 项目文件中正确配置了生成XML文档文件
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net5.0</TargetFramework>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule requires each project to be configured to include an XML documentation file as part of the compiled output. If the project configuration disables the XML comment analysis, it will lead to unchecked documentation comment semantics, increasing the likelihood of errors over time.

## Rule Meaning
Disabling the output of XML documentation files may lead to neglecting potential issues related to XML documentation comments, thus affecting code quality and documentation consistency.

## Error Example
```csharp
// The project file does not set XML documentation file generation
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net5.0</TargetFramework>
    <!-- No GenerateDocumentationFile setting -->
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
// The project file is correctly configured to generate an XML documentation file
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net5.0</TargetFramework>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```
rules.description: 当编译项目时，如果一个或多个文件的DocumentationMode设置为None，出现此规则的违规。应该配置每个项目以包含XML文档文件。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a compilation project contains one or more files with DocumentationMode set to None. Each project should be configured to include an XML documentation file.

rules.name: 逗号间距规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#代码文件中，逗号周围的间距不正确会违规。逗号后应跟随一个空格，除非在以下情况：

* 逗号可以出现在行尾
* 在`typeof`表达式的开放泛型类型中使用时，逗号后不跟随空格
* 逗号是字符串插值对齐组件的一部分。例如：`${x,3}`

## 规则意义
正确的代码格式能够提高代码的可读性和一致性，方便团队协作和代码维护。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
int[] numbers = {1,2,3,4};
var result = string.Format("{0},{1}", value1,value2);
'''
以上代码中，逗号后的空格缺失。

## 正确示例
'''csharp
int[] numbers = {1, 2, 3, 4};
var result = string.Format("{0}, {1}", value1, value2);
'''
此处每个逗号后都有一个空格。
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
A violation of spacing around a comma will occur within a C# code file. A comma should be followed by a single space, except in the following cases:

* A comma may appear at the end of a line
* No space is required following a comma when used in an open generic type in a `typeof` expression
* A comma is part of a string interpolation alignment component, e.g., `${x,3}`

## Rule Meaning
Proper code formatting enhances readability and consistency, facilitating team collaboration and code maintenance.

## Error Example
'''csharp
int[] numbers = {1,2,3,4};
var result = string.Format("{0},{1}", value1,value2);
'''
In the above code, spaces after commas are missing.

## Correct Example
'''csharp
int[] numbers = {1, 2, 3, 4};
var result = string.Format("{0}, {1}", value1, value2);
'''
Here, there is a space after each comma.
rules.description: 在C#代码文件中，逗号周围的间距不正确会导致违规。
rules.description_en: The spacing around a comma is incorrect, within a C# code file.

rules.name: 符号间隔规范
rules.content:

rules.description: 当操作符号的间隔不符合要求时，会违反此规则。

rules.name: 预处理器关键字前不应有空格
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则检查预处理器指令中的关键字前是否存在空格。例如：在 `# if Debug` 这种情况下，`#` 后的空格会导致违反此规则。

## 规则意义
遵循此规则可以确保代码的一致性和可读性，避免因空格导致的潜在解析错误。

## 错误示例
```csharp
# if Debug
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
#if Debug
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule checks if there is a space preceding the keyword in a preprocessor directive. For example, having a space in `# if Debug` causes a violation of this rule.

## Rule Meaning
Following this rule ensures code consistency and readability, preventing potential parsing errors caused by spaces.

## Error Example
```csharp
# if Debug
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
#if Debug
```
rules.description: 当预处理器指令中的关键字之前存在空格时违反此规则。确保关键字前没有空格。
rules.description_en: This rule is violated when there is a space preceding the keyword in a preprocessor directive. Ensure there is no space before the keyword.

rules.name: 运算符关键词后需有空格
rules.description: 当运算符重载方法中的operator关键词未被空格跟随时，会违反该规则。所有的operator关键词应当始终被一个空格跟随。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the operator keyword within an operator overload method is not followed by any whitespace. The operator keyword should always be followed by a single space.

rules.name: 开括号空格规范
rules.description: 当C#语句中的开括号前后空格不符合规定时会产生违规。确保开括号的空格符合规则以解决此问题。
rules.description_en: A violation occurs when the whitespace around an opening parenthesis in a C# statement is not correct. To resolve this, ensure the spacing follows the rule.

rules.name: 圆括号闭合空格规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#语句中，圆括号的闭合部分应正确使用空格。

## 规则意义
确保代码格式统一，提高代码可读性，减少误解和错误的可能性。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
int sum = (a + b )* c;
int value = (a + b);return value;
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
int sum = (a + b) * c;
int value = (a + b); return value;
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In a C# statement, the closing parenthesis should be spaced correctly.

## Rule Meaning
Ensures consistent code formatting, improves readability, and reduces the possibility of misunderstandings and errors.

## Error Example
'''csharp
int sum = (a + b )* c;
int value = (a + b);return value;
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
int sum = (a + b) * c;
int value = (a + b); return value;
'''
rules.description: C#语句中的圆括号闭合部分的空格不正确
rules.description_en: A closing parenthesis within a C# statement is not spaced correctly

rules.name: 方括号空格规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则要求在C#语句中，方括号与其周围的字符之间不能存在多余的空格。

## 规则意义
避免在方括号前后出现不必要的空格，以提高代码的可读性和一致性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
int[]  array = new int[ 5 ]; // [之前有空格，错误
int  	[] array = new int[5]; // []之间有多个空格，错误
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
int[] array = new int[5];
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule requires that square brackets within a C# statement should not be surrounded by unnecessary whitespace.

## Rule Meaning
Avoid unnecessary whitespace around square brackets to improve code readability and consistency.

## Error Example
```csharp
int[]  array = new int[ 5 ]; // Incorrect spacing before and after [
int  	[] array = new int[5]; // Incorrect spacing between []
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
int[] array = new int[5];
```
rules.description: 此规则在C#语句中的方括号前后不应有空格。
rules.description_en: An opening square bracket within a C# statement should not be preceded or followed by whitespace.

rules.name: 方括号闭合符号的空格使用规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#代码中，方括号闭合符号的前后空格使用不正确将违反此规则。

## 规则意义
遵循此规则有助于保持C#代码的一致性和可读性，避免因空格使用不当导致代码难以维护或理解。

## 错误示例
```csharp
int[] array = new int[5];
int value = array[ 0 ]; // 错误：方括号前后有空格
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
int[] array = new int[5];
int value = array[0]; // 正确：方括号前后没有不必要的空格
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule is violated when the spacing around a closing square bracket in C# code is incorrect.

## Rule Meaning
Adhering to this rule helps maintain consistency and readability of C# code, avoiding maintenance or comprehension difficulties due to improper spacing.

## Error Example
```csharp
int[] array = new int[5];
int value = array[ 0 ]; // Error: Spaces around brackets
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
int[] array = new int[5];
int value = array[0]; // Correct: No unnecessary spaces around brackets
```
rules.description: 当C#语句中的方括号闭合符号的空格使用不正确时，将违反此规则。方括号的前后空格应符合特定要求以保持代码的清晰度和一致性。
rules.description_en: This rule is violated when the spacing around a closing square bracket in a C# statement is incorrect. The spaces around the bracket should conform to specific guidelines to maintain clarity and consistency in the code.

rules.name: 大括号空格规范
rules.description: 当C#元素中的大括号周围的空格不正确时，会触发此规则。大括号应始终在前面有一个空格，除非它是行上的第一个字符，或者前面有一个开括号，此时括号和大括号之间不应有空格。大括号后应该始终跟随一个空格，除非它是行上的最后一个字符。
rules.description_en: This rule is triggered when the spacing around an opening brace within a C# element is incorrect. An opening brace should always be preceded by a single space unless it is the first character on the line or unless it is preceded by an opening parenthesis, in which case there should be no space between the parenthesis and the brace. An opening brace should always be followed by a single space unless it is the last character on the line.

rules.name: 大括号位置规则
rules.description: 该规则用于确保C#中的结束大括号使用正确的空格规则，从而提高代码的可读性和一致性。
rules.description_en: This rule ensures that closing braces in C# use the correct spacing rules to improve code readability and consistency.

rules.name: 泛型尖括号空格格式
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#中，开头泛型尖括号周围不应有空格，除非尖括号是行中的第一个或最后一个字符。

## 规则意义
保持代码风格一致，提高代码可读性和可维护性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
List <int> numbers = new List <int>();
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
List<int> numbers = new List<int>();
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In C#, there should be no whitespace around opening generic brackets, unless the bracket is the first or last character on the line.

## Rule Meaning
Maintain consistent code style to improve code readability and maintainability.

## Error Example
```csharp
List <int> numbers = new List <int>();
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
List<int> numbers = new List<int>();
```
rules.description: 当C#元素中的开头泛型尖括号的空格不正确时，会出现该规则的违规。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the spacing around an opening generic bracket within a C# element is not correct.

rules.name: 闭合泛型括号空格规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则确保闭合的泛型括号在C#代码中的空格使用符合规定。

## 规则意义
正确的空格使用可以提高代码的可读性和一致性，使代码更易于维护和理解。

## Rule Meaning
Proper spacing enhances code readability and consistency, making it easier to maintain and understand.

## Error Example
```csharp
List<int > myList = new List<int>();
Dictionary<string, List<int> > myDict = new Dictionary<string, List<int>>();
```

rules.description: 在C#元素中闭合的泛型括号未按规定间距使用。
rules.description_en: A closing generic bracket within a C# element is not spaced correctly.

rules.description: 本规则在属性括号开头后不应有空格，除非该括号是行的最后一个字符。

rules.description: 当C#元素内的关闭属性括号前的空格不正确时，会违规。
