rules.name: 可空类型符号前禁止空格
rules.content:
# 规则概述
本规则定义了C#语言中的可空类型符号应该如何正确使用空格。

## 规则意义
此规则确保代码风格的一致性，并提升代码的可读性。通过消除不必要的空白字符，代码显得更加紧凑和专业。

## 错误示例
```csharp
int? x = null;  // 正确
int ? y = null; // 错误: 可空类型符号 '?' 前不应有空格
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
int? x = null; // 正确：在可空类型符号 '?' 前没有空格
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule defines how whitespace should be used around nullable type symbols in C#.

## Rule Meaning
The rule ensures consistency in code style and improves readability. By removing unnecessary whitespace, the code appears more compact and professional.

## Error Example
```csharp
int? x = null;  // Correct
int ? y = null; // Error: There should be no space before the nullable type symbol '?'
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
int? x = null; // Correct: No space before the nullable type symbol '?'
```
rules.description: 在C#代码元素中，如果可空类型符号前存在空格，将违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when there is whitespace before a nullable type symbol within a C# element.

rules.name: 成员访问符号间距规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#代码文件中，成员访问符号 (通常是点号 “.”) 两侧的间距不当会触发本规则。正常情况下，成员访问符号的两侧不应有空格，除非它是行首的第一个字符。

## 规则意义
正确的间距可以提高代码的可读性和一致性，使代码看起来更加整洁和专业。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
var value = obj .Method();
var anotherValue = obj.Method() ;
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
var value = obj.Method();
var anotherValue = obj.Method();
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule is violated when the spacing around a member access symbol in a C# code file is incorrect. A member access symbol should not have whitespace on either side, unless it is the first character on the line.

## Rule Meaning
Correct spacing enhances code readability and consistency, making the code appear cleaner and more professional.

## Error Example
'''csharp
var value = obj .Method();
var anotherValue = obj.Method() ;
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
var value = obj.Method();
var anotherValue = obj.Method();
'''
rules.description: 在C#代码文件中，成员访问符号两侧的间距不当。
rules.description_en: The spacing around a member access symbol is incorrect, within a C# code file.

rules.name: 自增自减符号间距规范
rules.description: 此规则检查自增自减符号与该操作符的操作项之间是否有不必要的空格。
rules.description_en: This rule checks for unnecessary spaces between increment/decrement symbols and the items they operate on.

rules.name: 负号间距规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则要求C#代码中的负号在使用时必须满足特定的间距要求。

## 规则意义
正确使用间距可提高代码的可读性和可维护性，避免因格 式混乱导致的理解偏差。

## 错误示例
```csharp
int value = 5 -3;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
int value = 5 - 3;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule requires that negative signs in C# code adhere to specific spacing requirements.

## Rule Meaning
Correct use of spacing improves code readability and maintainability, and prevents misunderstandings due to misaligned formatting.

## Error Example
```csharp
int value = 5 -3;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
int value = 5 - 3;
```
rules.description: 当负号在C#元素中使用时，间距需要符合特定的要求。
rules.description_en: When a negative sign is used within a C# element, spacing must meet specific requirements.

rules.name: 正负号间距规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
该规则确保C#代码中的正号（+）符号周围的空格使用符合规范。

## 规则意义
正确的空格使用可以提高代码的可读性，使其更易于维护和理解。这一规则帮助开发者保持一致的代码风格，从而提高代码质量。

## 错误示例
```csharp
int x= +5;  // 错误：+前没有空格
int y = 5 +  7;  // 错误：+后有多余空格
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
int x = +5;
int y = 5 + 7;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule ensures that the spaces around positive signs (+) in C# code are used correctly.

## Rule Meaning
Proper use of spaces can improve the readability of the code, making it easier to maintain and understand. This rule helps developers maintain a consistent coding style, thereby improving code quality.

## Error Example
```csharp
int x= +5;  // Error: No space before +
int y = 5 +  7;  // Error: Extra space after +
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
int x = +5;
int y = 5 + 7;
```
rules.description: C#元素中的正号周围的间距不正确时会触发此规则。
rules.description_en: This rule is violated when the spacing around a positive sign in a C# element is incorrect.

rules.name: 解引用和地址符号间距规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#元素中，解引用符号或地址符号的间距不正确。

## 规则意义
正确的符号间距可以提高代码的可读性和可维护性，避免因为符号位置不当而造成的逻辑错误。

## 错误示例
```csharp
y=*x;
object *x = null;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
object* x = null;
y = *x;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
A dereference symbol or an access-of symbol within a C# element is not spaced correctly.

## Rule Meaning
Proper symbol spacing enhances readability and maintainability, preventing logical errors due to improper symbol positioning.

## Error Example
```csharp
y=*x;
object *x = null;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
object* x = null;
y = *x;
```
rules.description: C#元素中的解引用符号或地址符号的间距不正确。
rules.description_en: A dereference symbol or an access-of symbol within a C# element is not spaced correctly.

rules.name: 冒号间距规范
rules.description: 此规则用于确保 C# 代码中的冒号使用正确的间距格式。
rules.description_en: This rule ensures that colons in C# code are spaced correctly.

rules.name: 代码中不能包含连续多余的空格
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则要求代码中不应出现连续的多余空格字符，除非这些空格位于代码行的开头或结尾处，或紧跟在逗号或分号之后。

## 规则意义
保持代码风格的一致性，使代码更易于阅读和维护。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
int  i =  5;  // 不正确：多个空格
string  name = "John";  // 不正确：多个空格
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
int i = 5; // 正确：单个空格
string name = "John"; // 正确：单个空格
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule requires that code must not contain multiple whitespace characters in a row, unless these characters come at the beginning or end of a line of code, or following a comma or semicolon.

## Rule Meaning
Ensures consistent code style, making the code more readable and maintainable.

## Error Example
'''csharp
int  i =  5;  // Incorrect: multiple spaces
string  name = "John";  // Incorrect: multiple spaces
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
int i = 5; // Correct: single space
string name = "John"; // Correct: single space
'''
rules.description: 此规则会在代码中出现连续多个空格字符时触发警告，除了位于代码行的开头或结尾，或紧跟逗号或分号之后的情况。
rules.description_en: This rule triggers a warning when multiple whitespace characters appear consecutively in code, except when at the start or end of a line, or following a comma or semicolon.

rules.name: 隐式类型数组分配中的空格格式
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#代码文件中进行隐式类型数组分配时，不应在`new`或`stackalloc`关键字和紧随其后的数组括号之间出现空格。

## 规则意义
确保代码格式的一致性和可读性，并符合编码标准。

## 错误示例
```csharp
var a = new [] { 1, 10, 100, 1000 };
Span<int> b = stackalloc [] { 1, 10, 100, 1000 };
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
var a = new[] { 1, 10, 100, 1000 };
Span<int> b = stackalloc[] { 1, 10, 100, 1000 };
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Within a C# code file, an implicitly typed array allocation should not contain a space between the `new` or `stackalloc` keyword and the opening array bracket.

## Rule Meaning
This ensures consistent code formatting and readability according to coding standards.

## Error Example
```csharp
var a = new [] { 1, 10, 100, 1000 };
Span<int> b = stackalloc [] { 1, 10, 100, 1000 };
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
var a = new[] { 1, 10, 100, 1000 };
Span<int> b = stackalloc[] { 1, 10, 100, 1000 };
```
rules.description: 当代码中包含隐式类型数组分配，而在`new`或`stackalloc`关键字和数组括号之间有空格时，违反此规则
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when there is a space between the `new` or `stackalloc` keyword and the opening bracket of an implicitly-typed array allocation.

rules.name: 正确使用制表符
rules.description: 当代码中有制表符或空格与当前项目设置不一致时，会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs whenever the code contains a tab or space character which is not consistent with the current project settings.

rules.name: 代码行尾不能有多余空白字符
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在代码行的末尾如果存在空格、制表符或其他空白字符，除了行结束字符外，都属于违规行为。这些多余空白在一些文本编辑器中可能被显示出来，或在开发者格式化文档时被移除，这会导致不必要的代码变动。一些差异比较工具甚至会突出显示这些尾随空白，鼓励开发者去除它们。

## 规则意义
去除代码行末尾的多余空白有助于代码的可读性和维护性。此外，清理尾随空白可以防止在代码合并时产生不必要的冲突，并保持代码库的一致性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
int value = 42; 
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
int value = 42;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
A violation of this rule occurs when a line of code ends with any form of whitespace other than the end of line character(s). These extra whitespaces can be shown in editors that display whitespace or cause unnecessary churn when developers format the document later. Some diff tools even highlight trailing whitespace to encourage developers to trim it.

## Rule Meaning
Removing trailing whitespace improves code readability and maintainability. Additionally, cleaning up trailing whitespace can prevent unnecessary conflicts during code merges and keep the codebase consistent.

## Error Example
```csharp
int value = 42; 
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
int value = 42;
```
rules.description: 代码行末尾的空白字符除了行结束符之外都被认为是多余的，因此违反了这种规范可能导致代码的可读性和维护性下降。
rules.description_en: Whitespace at the end of a line of code other than end of line characters is considered unnecessary, and violating this rule can lead to reduced readability and maintainability.

rules.name: 基础类调用修饰符规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在代码中从基类调用成员时，不应该使用`base.`前缀，除非在本地类中存在该成员的重写或实现。

## 规则意义
使用错误的调用方式可能会导致覆盖方法被忽略，从而引入潜在的bug。当在基类中定义一个虚方法但没有在衍生类中覆盖它时，使用`base.`前缀调用此方法是不必要且有风险的。

## 错误示例
```csharp
string name = base.JoinName("John", "Doe");
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
string name = this.JoinName("John", "Doe");
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
A call to a member from a base class should not be prefixed with `base.`, unless a local implementation of the member exists.

## Rule Meaning
Using incorrect call methods might cause overridden methods to be ignored, introducing potential bugs. When a virtual method is defined in base class and not overridden in the derived class, using `base.` prefix to call this method is unnecessary and risky.

## Error Example
```csharp
string name = base.JoinName("John", "Doe");
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
string name = this.JoinName("John", "Doe");
```
rules.description: 在没有本地实现时从基类调用成员不应该使用`base.`前缀。
rules.description_en: A call to a member from the base class should not begin with `base.` unless a local implementation exists.

rules.name: 实例成员调用前缀规范
rules.description: 违反此规则的情况是当代码调用本地类或基类的实例成员且未使用'this.'作为前缀时。例外情况是本地类成员覆盖基类成员，而代码意图直接调用基类成员时，可以使用'base.'而不是'this.'作为前缀。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs whenever the code contains a call to an instance member of the local class or a base class which is not prefixed with 'this.'. An exception to this rule occurs when there is a local override of a base class member, and the code intends to call the base class member directly, bypassing the local override, in which case, the call can be prefixed with 'base.' rather than 'this.'.

rules.name: 查询表达式格式规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
本规则要求在C#查询表达式中，每个子句应开始于上一个子句的同一行或紧接下一行。

## 规则意义
遵循该规则有助于提高代码的可读性和一致性，便于团队协作和代码维护。

## 错误示例
```csharp
object x = from num in numbers
    select num;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
object x = from num in numbers select num;
```
或者
```csharp
object x =
    from num
    in numbers
    select num;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule requires that in a C# query expression, each clause should begin on the same line as the previous clause or on the next line.

## Rule Meaning
Following this rule helps enhance code readability and consistency, facilitating team collaboration and code maintenance.

## Error Example
```csharp
object x = from num in numbers
    select num;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
object x = from num in numbers select num;
```
or
```csharp
object x =
    from num
    in numbers
    select num;
```
rules.description: 当查询表达式中的子句未在同一行或紧接下一行开始时，将违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a clause within a query expression does not begin on the same line as the previous clause, or on the line following the query clause.

rules.name: 查询子句格式规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#查询表达式中，每一个查询子句应该全部位于同一行，或者每个子句各自占据一个单独的行。

## 规则意义
适当地格式化查询子句可以提高代码的可读性，方便维护和理解。

## 错误示例
```csharp
object x = from num in numbers
    select num;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
object x = from num in numbers select num;
```
或者
```csharp
object x =
    from num in numbers
    select num;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Within C# query expressions, each clause should either be entirely placed on the same line or each clause should begin on its own line.

## Rule Meaning
Properly formatting query clauses improves code readability and makes it easier to maintain and understand.

## Error Example
```csharp
object x = from num in numbers
    select num;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
object x = from num in numbers select num;
```
or
```csharp
object x =
    from num in numbers
    select num;
```
rules.description: 当C#查询表达式中的子句未全部位于同一行或未单独占据各自的行时，会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the clauses within a C# query expression are not all placed on the same line or each clause is not placed on its own line.

rules.name: 查询子句格式规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#中的查询表达式中，一个查询子句通常不应与上一个跨多行的子句位于同一行。在编写代码时，每个查询子句都应位于单独的一行，以提高代码的可读性和维护性。

## 规则意义
这一规则有助于使代码更加清晰和易于维护，减少理解复杂查询语句时出现的困惑，确保代码风格的一致性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
var elementNames =
    from element in GetElements
    (
        12,
        45
    ) select element.Name;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
var elementNames =
    from element in GetElements
    (
        12,
        45
    )
    select element.Name;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In C# query expressions, a query clause should not be on the same line as the previous clause if the previous clause spans multiple lines. Each query clause should start on its own new line for better readability and maintainability.

## Rule Meaning
This rule helps make the code more readable and maintainable, reducing confusion when interpreting complex query statements and ensuring a consistent code style.

## Error Example
```csharp
var elementNames =
    from element in GetElements
    (
        12,
        45
    ) select element.Name;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
var elementNames =
    from element in GetElements
    (
        12,
        45
    )
    select element.Name;
```
rules.description: 在C#查询表达式中，如果前一个子句跨多行，下一个子句不应位于同一行。
rules.description_en: In a C# query expression, the next clause should not be on the same line if the previous clause spans multiple lines.

rules.name: 查询子句格式规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#查询表达式中，当一个查询子句跨越多行时，它应该从新的一行开始，以提高代码可读性和一致性。

## 规则意义
这个规则能够帮助开发者保持代码风格的一致性，增强代码的可读性和维护性，使代码更易于理解和管理。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
var elementDescriptions =
    from element in elements select GenerateElementDescription
    (
        element
    );
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
var elementDescriptions =
    from element in elements
    select GenerateElementDescription
    (
        element
    );
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In C# query expressions, when a query clause spans multiple lines, it should start on a new line to improve code readability and consistency.

## Rule Meaning
This rule helps developers maintain consistent code style and enhances the readability and maintainability of code, making it easier to understand and manage.

## Error Example
'''csharp
var elementDescriptions =
    from element in elements select GenerateElementDescription
    (
        element
    );
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
var elementDescriptions =
    from element in elements
    select GenerateElementDescription
    (
        element
    );
'''
rules.description: 当查询子句跨越多行时，如果其没有单独从新行开始则违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a query clause spans multiple lines, but does not begin on its own line.

rules.name: 代码中不应包含空语句
rules.description: 代码不应该包含额外的分号，因为它们可能会导致空语句，这在逻辑上无意义，并可能降低代码的可读性和维护性。
rules.description_en: Code should not contain extra semicolons as they may lead to empty statements, which are logically meaningless and may decrease code readability and maintainability.

rules.name: 代码行分隔
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则要求每行代码只能包含一个语句。在同一行中编写多个语句会降低代码的可读性和可维护性。

## 规则意义
每个独立的语句其意义和逻辑都更加清晰。当每行只包含一个语句时，代码更易于阅读和理解，这也有助于在代码审查时更容易发现问题。

## 错误示例
```csharp
int a = 1; a++; int b = a;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
int a = 1;
a++;
int b = a;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule requires that each line of code contain only one statement. Writing multiple statements on the same line can reduce the readability and maintainability of the code.

## Rule Meaning
Each statement is clearer and more logical when presented separately. Having only one statement per line makes the code easier to read and understand, which also helps in code review processes to spot issues more easily.

## Error Example
```csharp
int a = 1; a++; int b = a;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
int a = 1;
a++;
int b = a;
```
rules.description: 代码行内不应包含多个语句。这一规则的违规发生在代码行内包含多个语句时。每个语句都应该从新的一行开始。
rules.description_en: Code must not contain multiple statements on one line. A violation of this rule occurs when the code contains more than one statement on a single line. Each statement should begin on a new line.

rules.name: 块语句不得包含嵌入式注释
rules.description: 当代码在语句声明和开括号之间包含注释时，将违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a comment is present between the declaration of a statement and the opening brace.

rules.name: 括号位置规范
rules.description: 在C#方法或索引器的调用或声明中，左括号或方括号没有放在方法或索引器名称同一行。
rules.description_en: The opening parenthesis or bracket in a call to a C# method or indexer, or the declaration of a method or indexer, is not placed on the same line as the method or indexer name.

rules.name: 闭合括号格式化规范
rules.description: 此规则检查C#方法或索引器调用或声明中的闭合括号是否位于最后一个参数的同一行。
rules.description_en: This rule checks if the closing parenthesis or bracket in a C# method or indexer call or declaration is placed on the same line as the last parameter.

rules.name: 圆括号闭合位置规范
rules.description: 当方法或索引器没有参数时，调用或声明的闭合括号应该与开括号在同一行。
rules.description_en: When a method or indexer has no parameters, the closing bracket in a call or declaration should be on the same line as the opening bracket.

rules.name: 逗号位置规范
rules.description: 在C#方法或索引器的参数之间，逗号未与前一个参数放在同一行。
rules.description_en: A violation occurs when a comma between parameters in a C# method or indexer is not placed on the same line as the previous parameter.

rules.name: 方法参数列表格式规范
rules.description: 方法或索引器调用或声明的参数列表起始位置必须与开头括号位于同一行或紧随其后的一行。
rules.description_en: The start of the parameter list for a method or indexer call or declaration must either be on the same line as the opening bracket or immediately after it.

rules.name: 参数格式规范
rules.description: 此规则检查C#方法或索引器调用或声明中的参数格式要求，使每个参数的书写风格保持一致。
rules.description_en: This rule checks the parameter format in C# method or indexer calls or declarations to ensure consistent styling.

rules.name: 方法参数分行规范
rules.description: 当方法或索引器的参数跨越多行时，第一个参数必须在括号后的下一行开始，以提升代码的可读性。
rules.description_en: When the parameters of a method or indexer span multiple lines, the first parameter must start on the line after the opening bracket to improve code readability.

rules.name: 方法参数格式规范
rules.description: 当方法或索引器的参数不全在同一行或者每个参数不各占一行时，就会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the parameters to a method or indexer are not all on the same line or each on its own line.

rules.name: 方法参数单行规范
rules.description: 为了避免方法调用变得过于复杂和不可读，除第一个参数外，其它参数应放在单行。个别情况下可例外。
rules.description_en: To prevent method calls from becoming excessively complicated and unreadable, parameters other than the first parameter should be placed on a single line, with specific exceptions.

rules.name: 语句不应使用不必要的括号
rules.description: 在不必要的情况下使用括号会导致代码可读性降低，应该去除这些多余的括号。
rules.description_en: Using parenthesis unnecessarily reduces code readability and they should be removed.

rules.name: 注释需包含文本
rules.description: 当代码包含不含任何文本的C#注释时，将违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs whenever the code contains a C# comment which does not contain any text.

rules.name: 使用内置类型别名
rules.description: 此规则要求在使用C#的基本类型时使用内置的类型别名，而不是类型名称或完全限定类型名称。
rules.description_en: This rule requires using the built-in type alias when using C# basic types instead of the type name or the fully qualified type name.

rules.name: 使用string.Empty替代空字符串
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议在代码中使用`string.Empty`替代硬编码的空字符串`""`。

## 规则意义
使用`string.Empty`可以提高代码的可读性和维护性，并防止多次在内存中创建相同的字符串。

## 错误示例
```csharp
string s = "";
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
string s = string.Empty;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule suggests using `string.Empty` instead of a hard-coded empty string `""` in the code.

## Rule Meaning
Using `string.Empty` can improve code readability and maintainability, and it prevents multiple instances of the same string from being created in memory.

## Error Example
```csharp
string s = "";
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
string s = string.Empty;
```
rules.description: 当代码中包含空字符串时，会违反此规则。建议使用string.Empty来替代硬编码的空字符串。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the code contains an empty string. It is recommended to use string.Empty instead of a hard-coded empty string.

rules.name: 不要在代码元素中使用区域
rules.description: 在代码元素中使用region会导致代码可读性差，因为这些区域通常是折叠的，隐藏了重要的代码细节。
rules.description_en: Using regions within code elements reduces code readability as those regions are often collapsed, hiding crucial code details.

rules.name: 避免使用代码区域块
rules.description: 此规则检查代码中是否存在区域块，并建议删除这些区域块，以提升代码的可读性。
rules.description_en: This rule checks for the presence of regions in the code and suggests removing them to enhance code readability.

rules.name: 使用简化的可空类型表示法
rules.description: 当未使用简化的C#语法定义可空类型时，会出现此规则违规。例如，使用 `Nullable<DateTime>` 而不是推荐的 `DateTime?`。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs whenever the Nullable type has been defined without using the shorthand C# style. For example, using `Nullable<DateTime>` instead of the preferred `DateTime?`.

rules.name: 泛型类型约束独占行
rules.description: 当代码在类型或方法声明的同一行中包含一个或多个泛型约束的`where`子句时，就会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs whenever the code contains one or more `where` clauses containing generic type constraints on the same line as the type or method declaration itself.

rules.name: 构造函数初始化器应在单独的行上
rules.description: 当代码包含一个与构造函数声明位于同一行的构造函数初始化器时，将违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs whenever the code contains a constructor initializer that is on the same line as the constructor declaration.

rules.name: 避免使用默认值类型构造函数
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#编程中，创建值类型的默认实例时，不应该使用`new T()`语法。相反，应该使用`default(T)`语法来避免混淆。

## 规则意义
使用`new T()`创建值类型的默认实例可能导致潜在的误解，尤其是在处理不可变值类型时。这种语法会使开发者认为他们创建了一个新的实例，而实际上只是被赋予了一个默认实例，进一步使用可能引发`NullReferenceException`。

## 错误示例
```csharp
ImmutableArray<int> array = new ImmutableArray<int>();
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
ImmutableArray<int> array = default(ImmutableArray<int>);
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In C# programming, it's not recommended to create a default instance of a value type using the `new T()` syntax. Instead, use the `default(T)` syntax to avoid confusion.

## Rule Meaning
Using `new T()` to create a default instance of a value type might cause potential misunderstandings, especially when dealing with immutable value types. This syntax might lead developers to think they have created a new instance, while in fact, it has only been assigned a default instance, leading to possible `NullReferenceException` upon further use.

## Error Example
```csharp
ImmutableArray<int> array = new ImmutableArray<int>();
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
ImmutableArray<int> array = default(ImmutableArray<int>);
```
rules.description: 当使用值类型时，应避免使用`new T()`来创建默认实例，而应使用等效的`default(T)`语法。
rules.description_en: When dealing with value types, avoid using `new T()` to create default instances. Use the equivalent `default(T)` syntax instead.

rules.name: 使用Lambda语法替换匿名方法
rules.description: 此规则要求使用Lambda表达式替代匿名方法以提升代码可读性和简洁性。
rules.description_en: This rule requires replacing anonymous methods with Lambda expressions to enhance code readability and conciseness.

rules.name: 使用可读性高的条件表达式
rules.description: 在比较表达式中，当左侧是文字或常量值时，应将变量放在左侧以提高可读性。
rules.description_en: In comparison expressions, when the left side is a literal or constant value, the variable should be placed on the left side to improve readability.

rules.name: 字段独立声明规范
rules.description: 当在同一个字段声明语法中声明两个或多个字段时，会产生此规则的违规。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when two or more fields are declared in the same field declaration syntax.

rules.name: 不要组合使用特性
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#代码中，不应将多个特性组合在同一对中括号内。

## 规则意义
将特性分开放置有助于提高代码的可读性和可维护性，使其更容易进行版本控制和差异比较。

## 错误示例
```csharp
[ExportCodeFixProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(MyCodeFixProvider)), Shared]
public class MyCodeFixProvider : CodeFixProvider
{
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
[ExportCodeFixProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(MyCodeFixProvider))]
[Shared]
public class MyCodeFixProvider : CodeFixProvider
{
}
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In C# code, multiple attributes should not be combined within a single set of square brackets.

## Rule Meaning
Separating attributes improves code readability and maintainability, making version control and diff comparisons easier.

## Error Example
```csharp
[ExportCodeFixProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(MyCodeFixProvider)), Shared]
public class MyCodeFixProvider : CodeFixProvider
{
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
[ExportCodeFixProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(MyCodeFixProvider))]
[Shared]
public class MyCodeFixProvider : CodeFixProvider
{
}
```
rules.description: 在同一对中括号内放置两个或更多特性违反了此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when two or more attributes are placed within the same set of square brackets.

rules.name: 属性分行规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则要求代码中的每个特性（attribute）应该单独占一行。将多个特性或特性与其他元素放置在同一行上会违反此规则。

## 规则意义
属性分行可以提高代码的可读性，使代码更清晰、更易于维护，特别是在有多个属性修饰同一元素的情况下。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
[ExportCodeFixProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(MyCodeFixProvider))][Shared]
public class MyCodeFixProvider : CodeFixProvider
{
}
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
[ExportCodeFixProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(MyCodeFixProvider))]
[Shared]
public class MyCodeFixProvider : CodeFixProvider
{
}
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule requires that each attribute in the code should be placed on its own line. Placing multiple attributes or an attribute with another element on the same line will violate this rule.

## Rule Meaning
Placing attributes on separate lines can improve the readability of the code, making it clearer and easier to maintain, especially when multiple attributes are used to annotate the same element.

## Error Example
'''csharp
[ExportCodeFixProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(MyCodeFixProvider))][Shared]
public class MyCodeFixProvider : CodeFixProvider
{
}
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
[ExportCodeFixProvider(LanguageNames.CSharp, Name = nameof(MyCodeFixProvider))]
[Shared]
public class MyCodeFixProvider : CodeFixProvider
{
}
'''
rules.description: 当多个特性被放置在同一行代码中，或特性与其他元素放置在同一行代码中时，将违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when two or more attributes are placed on the same line of code, or an attribute is placed on the same line as another element.

rules.name: using指令需使用完整命名空间
rules.description: 当using指令位于命名空间内且未使用完整命名空间名称，触发此规则。
rules.description_en: This rule is triggered when a using directive is contained within a namespace and is not fully qualified.

rules.name: 枚举值单独行规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则要求枚举中的每个值都应位于单独的行上。目的是提高代码的可读性，使代码更规范化，便于后续的维护和扩展。

## 规则意义
保持严格的一致性和代码规范有助于提高代码的可读性和可维护性。这不仅在团队协作时尤为重要，还能帮助开发者快速理解和识别枚举中的每个值。

## 错误示例
```csharp
public enum ExampleEnum
{
    FirstValue, SecondValue
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
public enum ExampleEnum
{
    FirstValue,
    SecondValue
}
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule requires each enum value to be placed on a separate line to enhance readability and maintainability of the code.

## Rule Meaning
Maintaining strict consistency and code conventions helps improve code readability and maintainability. This is especially important in team collaboration and helps developers quickly understand and identify each value in the enum.

## Error Example
```csharp
public enum ExampleEnum
{
    FirstValue, SecondValue
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
public enum ExampleEnum
{
    FirstValue,
    SecondValue
}
```
rules.description: 此规则要求枚举中的每个值都应位于单独的行上，以提高代码的可读性。
rules.description_en: This rule requires each enum value to be placed on a separate line to enhance code readability.

rules.name: 元素缩进一致性
rules.description: 当两个或多个同级元素各自占用自己的行但缩进不一致时，会违反此规则。修复方法是调整同级元素的缩进以使其一致。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when two or more sibling elements each start on their own line but are not indented the same amount. To fix the violation, adjust the indentation of sibling elements to match.

rules.name: 使用字面量后缀而不是显式类型转换
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#代码中，应使用字面量后缀而不是显式类型转换来表示特定类型的数字字面量。

## 规则意义
使用字面量后缀可以提高代码的可读性，并且减少错误的可能性。它使得代码的一目了然，不需要额外的类型转换步骤。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
var x = (long)1;
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
var x = 1L;
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In C# code, literals suffix notation should be used instead of explicit casting to represent specific types of number literals.

## Rule Meaning
Using literals suffix improves code readability and reduces the possibility of errors. It makes the code clearer without the need for additional casting steps.

## Error Example
'''csharp
var x = (long)1;
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
var x = 1L;
'''
rules.description: 该规则要求使用字面量后缀而不是进行显式类型转换，以提高代码的可读性和减少错误。
rules.description_en: This rule requires the use of literals suffix notation instead of explicit casting to improve code readability and reduce errors.

rules.name: 使用元组语法
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则检查代码中是否使用了ValueTuple类型声明，而不是首选的元组语言结构。

## 规则意义
在C# 7及更高版本中，元组已被语言本身直接支持，使用元组语法可以提高代码的可读性和一致性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
ValueTuple<int, int> x; // SA1141
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
(int, int) x;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule checks if the code uses a ValueTuple type declaration instead of the preferred tuple language construct.

## Rule Meaning
In C# 7 and later, tuples are directly supported by the language, making the code more readable and consistent.

## Error Example
```csharp
ValueTuple<int, int> x; // SA1141
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
(int, int) x;
```
rules.description: 规则描述：代码中使用了ValueTuple类型声明，而不是首选的元组语言结构。
rules.description_en: Rule Description: A ValueTuple type declaration was used instead of the preferred tuple language construct.

rules.name: 使用元组元素名称引用
rules.content:
# 规则概述
当元组元素有名称可用时，不应通过其元数据名称引用。

## 规则意义
使用元组元素的名称而不是元数据名称可以提高代码的可读性和可维护性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
(int valueA, int valueB) x;

var y = x.Item1; // SA1142
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
(int valueA, int valueB) x;

var y = x.valueA;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Tuple elements should not be referenced by their metadata name when an element name is available.

## Rule Meaning
Using the element name instead of the metadata name improves code readability and maintainability.

## Error Example
```csharp
(int valueA, int valueB) x;

var y = x.Item1; // SA1142
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
(int valueA, int valueB) x;

var y = x.valueA;
```
rules.description: 当元组元素有名称可用时，不应通过其元数据名称引用。
rules.description_en: An element of a tuple was referenced by its metadata name when an element name is available.

rules.name: using指令放置位置规范
rules.description: 当using指令或using别名放置在命名空间元素之外时，就会出现此规则违规。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a using directive or a using-alias directive is placed outside of a namespace element.

rules.name: 代码元素顺序规范
rules.description: 文件中的代码元素未按照标准顺序进行排列。
rules.description_en: An element within a C# code file is out of order in relation to the other elements in the code.

rules.name: 成员访问级别排序
rules.description: 当C#代码文件中的元素没有按照访问级别的标准顺序进行排序时，会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the code elements within a file do not follow a standard ordering scheme based on access level.

rules.name: 常量与字段顺序规范
rules.description: 当常量字段位于非常量字段下面时，就会发生这种违规。常量应该位于字段上方，以表明这两者在编译器中是根本不同类型的元素，具有不同的考虑因素和命名要求。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a constant field is placed beneath a non-constant field. Constants should be placed above fields to indicate that the two are fundamentally different types of elements with different considerations for the compiler, different naming requirements, etc.

rules.name: 静态元素位置规范
rules.description: 在C#类中，所有静态元素应位于相同类型的实例元素之前。
rules.description_en: In a C# class, all static elements should appear before instance elements of the same type.

rules.name: 部分元素必须声明访问修饰符
rules.description: 当部分元素未定义访问修饰符时，违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the partial elements do not have an access modifier defined.

rules.name: 声明关键词顺序规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在元素声明中，关键词必须遵循标准的顺序进行排列。以确保代码的可读性和一致性。

## 规则意义
这个规则的重要性在于通过使用标准的关键词顺序，代码的访问级别能够一目了然，减少意外提高元素访问级别的风险。

## 错误示例
```csharp
public static int MyMethod() {}
private const static int MyConstant = 0;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
public static int MyMethod() {}
private static const int MyConstant = 0;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Within an element declaration, keywords must appear in a standard order to ensure code readability and consistency.

## Rule Meaning
The importance of this rule is that it makes the access level of each element clear at a glance, reducing the risk of accidentally increasing the access level of an element.

## Error Example
```csharp
public static int MyMethod() {}
private const static int MyConstant = 0;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
public static int MyMethod() {}
private static const int MyConstant = 0;
```
rules.description: 元素声明中的关键词没有按照标准的顺序排列。
rules.description_en: The keywords within the declaration of an element do not follow a standard ordering scheme.

rules.name: 访问修饰符顺序规范
rules.description: 代码中的访问修饰符使用顺序不正确，可能导致阅读障碍和误解。为了代码的一致性，*protected*应当在*internal*之前，*private*应当在*protected*之前。
rules.description_en: Incorrect order of access modifiers in code may lead to reading difficulties and misunderstandings. For code consistency, *protected* should precede *internal*, and *private* should precede *protected*.

rules.name: System命名空间优先使用
rules.content:
# 规则概述
该规则检查C#文件中的`using`指令是否将*System*命名空间放在其他命名空间之前，以确保代码的可读性和维护性。

## 规则意义
将*System*命名空间的`using`指令置于其他命名空间之上，有助于提高代码的清晰度，使开发人员更容易了解代码的依赖关系，并提高团队的代码协作效率。

## 错误示例
```csharp
using MyNamespace;
using System;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
using System;
using MyNamespace;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule checks whether `using` directives for the *System* namespace are placed before other namespaces in C# files to ensure code readability and maintainability.

## Rule Meaning
Placing `using` directives for the *System* namespace above those for other namespaces helps improve code clarity, making it easier for developers to understand code dependencies and enhancing team collaboration efficiency.

## Error Example
```csharp
using MyNamespace;
using System;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
using System;
using MyNamespace;
```
rules.description: 当*System*命名空间的`using`指令在其他命名空间`using`指令之后出现时，则违反了此规则。将所有*System*命名空间的`using`指令放在最前面，使代码更简洁易读，还可以使人更容易识别代码所使用的命名空间。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a `using` directive for the *System* namespace is placed after a non-*System* `using` directive. Placing all `using` directives for the *System* namespace at the top makes the code cleaner and easier to read, and helps make it easier to identify the namespaces being used by the code.

rules.name: using别名指令排序规范
rules.description: 当using别名指令位于普通using指令之前时，会出现该规则违规。将所有using别名指令放在所有普通using指令之下可以让代码更清晰和易于阅读，并有助于识别代码中使用的类型。
rules.description_en: A violation occurs when a using-alias directive is placed before a regular using directive. Placing all using-alias directives beneath all normal using directives can make the code cleaner and easier to read, and can help in identifying the types used throughout the code.

rules.name: using指令命名空间排序规范
rules.description: 当C#代码文件中的using指令没有按照字母顺序排列时，会违反此规则。System命名空间的指令始终应置于其他命名空间之前。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the using directives are not sorted alphabetically by namespace. The System namespaces should always precede all other namespaces.

rules.name: using别名按字母顺序排序
rules.description: 此规则检查C#代码中的using别名指令是否按别名名称的字母顺序排列，从而提高代码的可读性和整洁性。
rules.description_en: This rule checks that the using-alias directives in C# code are ordered alphabetically by alias name to enhance code readability and cleanliness.

rules.name: 属性访问器顺序规范
rules.description: 当属性或索引器中的`get`访问器在`set`或`init`访问器之后出现时，将违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a `get` accessor appears after a `set` or `init` accessor within a property or indexer.

rules.name: 事件访问器顺序
rules.description: 当事件中的`add`访问器位于`remove`访问器之后时，会违反此规则。为了符合此规则，`add`访问器应位于`remove`访问器之前。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when an `add` accessor is placed after a `remove` accessor within an event. To comply with this rule, the `add` accessor should be placed before the `remove` accessor.

rules.name: 只读元素位置规范
rules.description: 当一个只读字段位于一个非只读字段之下时，就会违反该规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a readonly field is positioned beneath a non-readonly field.

rules.name: using static指令位置规范
rules.description: 当using static指令的位置不正确时，会违反此规则。将using static指令放在普通using指令之后，别名using指令之前，可以使代码更清晰易读。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a using static directive is positioned at the wrong location. Placing the using static directives after regular and before alias using directives makes the code cleaner and easier to read.

rules.name: 静态引用按字母排序
rules.description: 当C#代码文件中的`using static`指令没有按完整类型名称的字母顺序排序时，会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the `using static` directives within a C# code file are not sorted alphabetically by the full type name.

rules.name: 元素名称大小写规则
rules.description: 此规则要求C#元素的名称必须以大写字母开头，包括命名空间、类、枚举、结构、委托、事件、方法、属性等。
rules.description_en: This rule requires that the names of C# elements must begin with an upper-case letter, including namespaces, classes, enums, structs, delegates, events, methods, and properties.

rules.name: 元素命名需以小写字母开头
rules.description: 该规则要求代码中的元素名称以小写字母开头，以保持代码的一致性和可读性。
rules.description_en: This rule requires that element names in the code begin with a lowercase letter to maintain consistency and readability of the code.

rules.name: 接口命名规则
rules.description: 当接口名称没有以大写字母I开头时违反此规则。接口名称应该总是以I开头。例如，ICustomer。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the name of an interface does not begin with the capital letter I. Interface names should always begin with I. For example, ICustomer.

rules.name: 常量命名规则
rules.description: 常量字段应该以大写字母开头。
rules.description_en: Constant fields should begin with an uppercase letter.

rules.name: 非私有只读字段命名规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
非私有的只读C#字段名称应以大写字母开头，确保代码的可读性和一致性。

## 规则意义
字段命名规范有助于提高代码的可读性，因为开发人员可以清楚地了解哪些字段是公共的或保护性的，并且不能被修改。遵循命名规范有助于维护代码的整体结构。

## 错误示例
```csharp
public readonly int exampleField;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
public readonly int ExampleField;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
The name of a non-private readonly C# field should begin with an upper-case letter to ensure readability and consistency in the code.

## Rule Meaning
Field naming conventions help in improving code readability, as developers can clearly understand which fields are public or protected and immutable. Adhering to naming conventions assists in maintaining the overall structure of the code.

## Error Example
```csharp
public readonly int exampleField;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
public readonly int ExampleField;
```
rules.description: 当非私有的只读字段名称不是以大写字母开头时违反此规则。非私有只读字段应该始终以大写字母开头。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the name of a readonly field which is not private does not begin with an upper-case letter. Non-private readonly fields should always start with an upper-case letter.

rules.name: 字段命名不使用匈牙利命名法
rules.content:
# 规则概述
本规则要求C#中的字段和变量名不应使用匈牙利命名法。匈牙利命名法在C++中较为常见，但在C#中提倡使用更长且更具描述性的变量名，这些变量名应根据其用途命名，而不是基于变量的类型。

## 规则意义
使用更具描述性的名称可以使代码更易读和维护。目前，大多数现代代码编辑器（如Visual Studio）都可以方便地通过悬停查看变量类型信息，因此不需要通过名称携带类型信息的匈牙利命名法。

## 错误示例
```csharp
int iCount = 0;
string strName = "example";
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
int count = 0;
string name = "example";
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule requires that fields and variables in C# should not use Hungarian notation. While Hungarian notation is common in C++ code, the trend in C# is to use longer, more descriptive names that describe what the variable is used for, rather than the type of the variable.

## Rule Meaning
Using more descriptive names improves the readability and maintainability of the code. Modern code editors, such as Visual Studio, make it easy to check type information by hovering over the variable, reducing the need for type-informative naming.

## Error Example
```csharp
int iCount = 0;
string strName = "example";
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
int count = 0;
string name = "example";
```
rules.description: 本规则用于限制C#的字段和变量名中使用匈牙利命名法。
rules.description_en: This rule restricts the use of Hungarian notation in C# field and variable names.

rules.name: 字段命名规范
rules.description: C#中的字段名称不以小写字母开头。
rules.description_en: The name of a field in C# does not begin with a lower-case letter.

rules.name: 字段命名规范
rules.description: 公共或内部字段的名称应以大写字母开头，以确保代码的一致性和可读性。如果名称需与Win32或COM相关项匹配，则可在*NativeMethods*类中使用小写。
rules.description_en: The name of a public or internal field should start with an uppercase letter to ensure code consistency and readability. If the name needs to match a Win32 or COM item, it can start with a lowercase letter if placed within a NativeMethods class.

rules.name: 变量命名规范
rules.description: 违反该规则的情况出现在字段名称以 *m_*、*s_* 或 *t_* 为前缀时。默认情况下，StyleCop 不允许使用下划线作为前缀，而建议使用 'this.'。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a field name is prefixed by *m_*, *s_*, or *t_*. By default, StyleCop disallows the use of underscores as prefixes and recommends using 'this.'.

rules.name: 字段命名不应以下划线开头
rules.description: 当字段名称以下划线开头时，会出现规则违规。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a field name begins with an underscore.

rules.name: 字段命名不应包含下划线
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则要求C#中的字段命名不能包含下划线。字段和变量应使用描述性和易读的名称来反映其功能，通常使用驼峰命名法，而不是下划线。

## 规则意义
遵循此命名规则可以提高代码的可读性和一致性，使开发者能够更容易地理解和维护代码。通过使用一致的命名标准，可以减少因命名不当引发的混淆或错误。

## 错误示例
```csharp
public class Customer
{
    private int customer_id; // 命名不当，包含下划线
}
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
public class Customer
{
    private int customerId; // 正确命名，采用驼峰命名法
}

public class Win32NativeMethods
{
    private int customer_id; // 对于Win32或COM相关的项，这是可以接受的
}
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule enforces that field names in C# should not contain underscores. Fields and variables should use descriptive and readable names that describe their function, typically using camel case rather than underscores.

## Rule Meaning
Adhering to this naming rule improves code readability and consistency, making it easier for developers to understand and maintain the code. By using a consistent naming standard, confusion or errors caused by improper naming can be minimized.

## Error Example
```csharp
public class Customer
{
    private int customer_id; // Incorrect naming, contains underscore
}
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
public class Customer
{
    private int customerId; // Correct naming using camel case
}

public class Win32NativeMethods
{
    private int customer_id; // Acceptable for Win32 or COM related items
}
```
rules.description: 规则定义要求字段名不应包含下划线，建议使用驼峰命名法以提高代码的可读性。
rules.description_en: The rule specifies that field names must not contain underscores and recommends using camel case to improve code readability.

rules.name: 静态只读字段命名规范
rules.description: 当静态只读字段的名称以小写字母开头时会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the name of a static readonly field begins with a lower-case letter.

rules.name: 变量命名规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
变量名称应以小写字母开头。此规则可提高代码的可读性和一致性。

## 规则意义
符合标准的变量命名约定能让代码更易理解，并且使代码在团队开发中更加一致。

## 错误示例
```csharp
int MyVariable = 10;
string ExampleString = "Hello World";
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
int myVariable = 10;
string exampleString = "Hello World";
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Variable names should begin with a lowercase letter. This rule enhances code readability and consistency.

## Rule Meaning
Adhering to standard variable naming conventions makes code easier to understand and more consistent in team development.

## Error Example
```csharp
int MyVariable = 10;
string ExampleString = "Hello World";
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
int myVariable = 10;
string exampleString = "Hello World";
```
rules.description:
如果变量名不是小写字母开头，则违反此规则。为了符合议定俗成的命名规则，建议将变量名改为以小写字母开头。
如果变量名称是为了匹配Win32或COM相关联的项，并且需要以大写字母开头，请将变量放在`NativeMethods`类内。`NativeMethods`类通常用于Win32或COM的包装器，在这种情况下StyleCop会忽略这个违规。
rules.description_en:
A violation of this rule occurs when the name of a variable does not begin with a lower-case letter. To conform to established naming conventions, it is recommended to change the variable name to start with a lower-case letter.
If the variable name is intended to match the name of an item associated with Win32 or COM, and thus needs to begin with an upper-case letter, place the variable within a `NativeMethods` class. A `NativeMethods` class is typically used for Win32 or COM wrappers, and StyleCop will ignore this violation.

rules.name: 方法参数命名规则
rules.description: 当方法的参数名称没有以小写字母开头时，就会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the name of a parameter does not begin with a lower-case letter.

rules.name: 类型参数命名规范
rules.description: 违反此规则的情况出现在C#类型参数名称不以大写字母T开头时。类型参数名称应始终以T开头，例如T或TKey。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the name of a C# type parameter does not begin with the capital letter T. Type parameter names should always begin with T. For example, T or TKey.

rules.name: 元组元素名称大小写规范
rules.description: 元组类型中的元素名称应使用正确的大小写。
rules.description_en: Element names within a tuple type should use the correct casing.

rules.name: 访问修饰符声明要求
rules.description: 此规则要求为每个元素显式定义访问修饰符，以提升代码可读性，避免使用者产生误解。
rules.description_en: This rule requires that an access modifier be explicitly stated for every element to enhance code readability and avoid misunderstanding.

rules.name: 字段访问修饰符规范
rules.description: 该规则要求类中的字段必须使用私有访问修饰符，旨在通过使用属性公开字段来提高代码的可维护性。
rules.description_en: This rule requires fields within a class to use private access modifiers, aiming to enhance code maintainability by using properties to expose fields.

rules.name: 文件中只能包含一个类型
rules.description: 如果一个C#文件中包含多个类型则会违反此规则。为了提高代码库的长期可维护性，每个类型应放置在自己的文件中，且文件名应反映文件中的类型名称。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a C# file contains more than one type. To increase long-term maintainability of the code-base, each type should be placed in its own file, and file names should reflect the name of the type within the file.

rules.name: 单一命名空间限制
rules.description: 此规则要求C#文件仅包含单个命名空间，以便于维护和提高代码可读性。
rules.description_en: This rule requires a C# file to contain only a single namespace to facilitate maintenance and improve code readability.

rules.name: 抑制消息必须提供理由
rules.description: 该规则要求在使用SuppressMessage属性时提供合理的理由。如果未提供理由，可能会影响代码的长期可维护性。
rules.description_en: This rule requires providing a justification when using the SuppressMessage attribute. Failure to provide a justification may affect the long-term maintainability of the code.

rules.name: Debug.Assert 必须提供描述性消息
rules.content:
# 规则概述
SA1405 规则要求在代码中使用 Debug.Assert 时，必须提供一个描述性的消息文本。这样可以在断言失败时，帮助用户理解错误的原因。

## 规则意义
当 Debug.Assert 语句触发时，带有描述性消息的断言能够更明确地说明问题所在，有助于问题的快速定位和修复。此外，描述性消息能够提升代码的可维护性，使代码逻辑更加清晰和自解释。

## 错误示例
```csharp
debug.Assert(value != true);
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
debug.Assert(value != true, "The value must always be true.");
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Rule SA1405 requires that Debug.Assert statements in code must provide a descriptive message to explain the context of the assertion. This helps users understand the issue better when an assertion fails.

## Rule Meaning
Having a descriptive message in Debug.Assert enhances understanding when the assertion triggers, aiding in faster issue resolution and increasing code maintainability. It allows the code logic to be more understandable and self-explanatory.

## Error Example
```csharp
debug.Assert(value != true);
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
debug.Assert(value != true, "The value must always be true.");
```
rules.description: 规则要求在 Debug.Assert 调用中提供描述性消息，以方便在断言失败时可以清楚地理解问题。
rules.description_en: The rule requires providing a descriptive message in Debug.Assert calls to clearly understand the problem when an assertion fails.

rules.name: Debug.Fail调用必须提供描述性信息
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#代码中，如果调用Debug.Fail而没有提供描述性信息，会导致违反此规则。提供描述信息可以帮助最终用户理解问题发生的原因。

## 规则意义
确保每个Debug.Fail调用都包含有意义的描述信息是良好的编码习惯。它不仅提高了代码的可维护性，也有助于调试和错误排查。

## 错误示例
```csharp
Debug.Fail();
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
Debug.Fail("此代码路径不应被执行。");
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
A violation of this rule occurs when a call to Debug.Fail in C# code does not include a descriptive message. Providing a descriptive message helps end users understand why the failure occurred.

## Rule Meaning
Ensuring that every Debug.Fail call includes a meaningful message is a good coding practice. It not only improves code maintainability but also aids in debugging and error investigation.

## Error Example
```csharp
Debug.Fail();
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
Debug.Fail("The code should never reach this point.");
```
rules.description: 在C#代码中调用Debug.Fail时需包含描述信息，方便用户理解问题。
rules.description_en: Calls to Debug.Fail in C# code must include a descriptive message to help users understand the issue.

rules.name: 算术表达式需声明运算优先级
rules.content:
# 规则概述
在C#中，算术运算符具有预定义的运算优先级。尽管允许在不使用括号的情况下将多个算术运算符混合使用，但这会降低代码的可读性和可维护性。强制使用括号清楚地声明运算顺序可以提高代码清晰度。

## 规则意义
为算术表达式添加括号可以减少读者对代码行为的误判风险，增强代码的可读性和维护性，从而减少后期可能引入错误的可能性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
int x = 5 + y * b / 6 % z - 2;
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
int x = 5 + (y * ((b / 6) % z)) - 2;
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
In C#, arithmetic operators have predefined precedence. It is legal to chain multiple arithmetic operations without using parentheses, but this decreases code readability and maintainability. Enforcing the use of parentheses to clearly declare the operation order enhances code clarity.

## Rule Meaning
Adding parentheses to arithmetic expressions reduces misinterpretation risks, enhances code readability and maintainability, thereby reducing the potential introduction of bugs.

## Error Example
```csharp
int x = 5 + y * b / 6 % z - 2;
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
int x = 5 + (y * ((b / 6) % z)) - 2;
```
rules.description: C#语句中包含复杂的算术表达式，但未在运算符周围添加括号。
rules.description_en: A C# statement contains a complex arithmetic expression which omits parenthesis around operators.

rules.name: 条件表达式括号优先级声明
rules.description: 此规则要求在复杂的条件表达式内使用括号，以明确运算符的优先级，从而提升代码的可读性和可维护性。
rules.description_en: This rule requires the use of parentheses in complex conditional expressions to explicitly declare operator precedence, thereby enhancing code readability and maintainability.

rules.name: 删除不必要的委托小括号
rules.content:
# 规则概述
此规则建议：当匿名方法不包含任何参数时，可以省略参数括号，以增强代码的可读性。

## 规则意义
在匿名方法中，如果没有参数，那么括号是可以省略的。去除多余的括号不仅使代码更简洁，而且容易阅读。

## 错误示例
```csharp
this.Method(delegate() { return 2; });
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
this.Method(delegate { return 2; });
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule suggests omitting the parentheses around the parameters when an anonymous method does not contain any, to improve code readability.

## Rule Meaning
In anonymous methods, if there are no parameters, the parentheses can be omitted. Removing unnecessary parentheses makes the code neater and easier to read.

## Error Example
```csharp
this.Method(delegate() { return 2; });
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
this.Method(delegate { return 2; });
```
rules.description: 当匿名方法不包含参数时，括号是可选的，建议删除不必要的括号。
rules.description_en: When an anonymous method does not contain any parameters, the parentheses are optional. It is recommended to remove unnecessary parentheses.

rules.name: 属性构造器的括号使用规范
rules.content:
# 规则概述
当属性声明没有包含任何参数时，属性构造器中的括号是可选的，但通常情况下不应被使用。

## 规则意义
去掉不必要的括号可以使代码更简洁，提高代码的可读性和可维护性。

## 错误示例
```csharp
[Serializable()]
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
[Serializable]
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
When an attribute declaration does not contain any parameters, the parenthesis in the attribute constructor are optional and typically should not be used.

## Rule Meaning
Removing unnecessary parenthesis can make the code cleaner and enhance readability and maintainability.

## Error Example
```csharp
[Serializable()]
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
[Serializable]
```
rules.description: 属性声明没有参数时，属性构造器中不应使用不必要的括号。
rules.description_en: Unnecessary parenthesis should not be used in an attribute constructor when the attribute declaration does not contain any parameters.

rules.name: 文件编码格式规范
rules.description: 该规则要求所有的源文件都使用包含字节顺序标记（BOM）的UTF-8编码格式，以确保编译器能一致处理文件。
rules.description_en: This rule requires all source files to use UTF-8 encoding with a byte order mark (BOM) to ensure consistent processing by the compiler.

rules.name: 使用尾随逗号规范多行初始化器
rules.content:
# 规则概述
SA1413规则要求在多行初始化器的最后一个语句后加上尾随逗号。这有助于代码版本管理中的审阅，避免在添加或删除行时产生不必要的变更。

## 规则意义
在多行初始化器使用尾随逗号可以减少合并冲突，提高代码可读性和一致性。

## 错误示例
'''csharp
var x = new Barnacle
{
    Age = 100,
    Height = 0.2M,
    Weight = 0.88M
};
'''

## 正确示例
'''csharp
var x = new Barnacle
{
    Age = 100,
    Height = 0.2M,
    Weight = 0.88M,
};
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Rule SA1413 requires adding a trailing comma to the last statement in a multi-line initializer. This assists in code reviews and reduces unnecessary modifications when adding or removing lines.

## Rule Meaning
Using trailing commas in multi-line initializers can reduce merge conflicts and improve code readability and consistency.

## Error Example
'''csharp
var x = new Barnacle
{
    Age = 100,
    Height = 0.2M,
    Weight = 0.88M
};
'''

## Correct Example
'''csharp
var x = new Barnacle
{
    Age = 100,
    Height = 0.2M,
    Weight = 0.88M,
};
'''
rules.description: 多行C#初始化器或列表的最后一个语句缺少尾随逗号，将导致此规则的违反。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the last statement of a C# initializer or list is missing a trailing comma.

rules.name: 元组类型命名规范
rules.description: 在成员声明中使用元组类型时，应该为每个元素提供明确的名称。
rules.description_en: Tuple types in member declarations should have explicitly named elements.

rules.name: 大括号换行规范
rules.description: 当语句、元素或表达式中包含大括号时，开闭括号需各占一行。
rules.description_en: Opening and closing braces in statements, elements, or expressions must be placed on their own lines.

rules.name: 语句格式规范
rules.description: 在使用大括号包裹的代码块中，不能将完整的语句写在一行内。
rules.description_en: A C# statement containing opening and closing braces should not be written completely on a single line.

rules.name: 元素不应在单行上
rules.description: 违反此规则的情况是元素在大括号内的代码被写在一行中。在代码中，方法、类或控制结构不应该在同一行中包含其所有大括号和实现。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when an element containing code within braces is written on a single line. Methods, classes, or control structures should not contain all their braces and implementation on a single line.

rules.name: 代码块花括号规范
rules.description: 当C#语句的花括号被省略时，会发生违反此规则的情况。虽然C#允许省略某些语句的花括号，但本规则始终要求使用花括号，以增加代码的可读性和可维护性。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the opening and closing braces for a C# statement have been omitted. Although C# allows the omission of braces for some statements, this rule mandates their presence to improve code readability and maintainability.

rules.name: 访问器格式一致性
rules.description: 此规则要求在属性、索引器或事件中，所有访问器应统一使用单行或多行格式书写，以提高代码的可读性。
rules.description_en: This rule requires that within properties, indexers, or events, all accessors should consistently use either single-line or multi-line formatting to enhance code readability.

rules.name: 大括号后不应有空行
rules.description: 为提高代码的可读性，StyleCop要求在某些情况下使用空行，并禁止在其他情况下使用空行。这使得代码在视觉上具有一致的模式，用以提高不熟悉代码的识别和可读性。
rules.description_en: To improve the readability of the code, StyleCop requires blank lines in certain situations and prohibits them in others, resulting in a consistent visual pattern that can enhance the recognition and readability of unfamiliar code.

rules.name: 元素文档注释头后不能跟随空行
rules.description: 当元素文档注释头后跟随一个空行时，会触发此规则的违规。为了提高代码的可读性，StyleCop 在某些情况下需要空行，而在其他情况下禁止空行。这确保了代码在视觉上的一致性，这有助于提高对不熟悉的代码的识别和可读性。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the element documentation header above an element is followed by a blank line. To improve the readability of the code, StyleCop requires blank lines in certain situations, and prohibits blank lines in other situations. This results in a consistent visual pattern across the code, which can improve recognition and readability of unfamiliar code.

rules.name: 代码格式规范
rules.description: 当C#代码中出现连续多个空行时违反此规则。要改善代码的可读性，StyleCop要求在某些情况下使用空行，并禁止在其他情况下使用空行。这为代码提供了一种一致的视觉模式，有助于提升对不熟悉代码的识别和可读性。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the C# code contains multiple blank lines in a row. StyleCop requires blank lines in certain situations to improve the readability of the code, and prohibits blank lines in other situations. This results in a consistent visual pattern across the code, which can improve the recognition and readability of unfamiliar code.

rules.name: 闭合大括号前不应有空行
rules.description: 为了提高代码的可读性，StyleCop要求在某些情况下使用空行，而在其他情况下禁止使用。违反此规则的情况是闭合大括号前存在空行。
rules.description_en: To improve code readability, StyleCop requires blank lines in certain situations and prohibits them in others. A violation of this rule occurs when a closing brace is preceded by a blank line.

rules.name: 代码块前不可有空行
rules.description: 为了提高代码的可读性，StyleCop要求在某些情况下需要添加空行，而在其他情况下禁止空行。规则SA1509不允许在大括号之前出现空行。
rules.description_en: To improve the readability of the code, StyleCop requires blank lines in certain situations, and prohibits blank lines in others. Rule SA1509 disallows blank lines before opening braces.

rules.name: 链式语句块不应以空行开头
rules.description: 为了提高代码的可读性，StyleCop要求在某些情况下使用空行，而在其他情况下禁止使用空行。某些链式C#语句块不应以空行分隔。
rules.description_en: To improve code readability, StyleCop requires blank lines in certain situations and prohibits them in others. Certain chained C# statement blocks must not be separated by a blank line.

rules.name: While-Do语句格式
rules.description: 当do-while语句中的while关键字与主体代码之间存在一个或多个空行时，会违反此规则，应移除空行以符合代码格式要求。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the while keyword at the bottom of a do-while statement is separated from the main part of the statement by one or more blank lines. Remove the blank lines to comply with code formatting requirements.

rules.name: 单行注释后不应有空行
rules.description: 为了提高代码可读性，StyleCop要求在某些情况下使用空行，而在其他情况下禁止空行。这导致代码中的视觉模式一致性，提高识别性和对不熟悉代码的可读性。
rules.description_en: To improve the readability of the code, StyleCop requires blank lines in certain situations and prohibits them in others. This results in a consistent visual pattern, improving recognition and readability of unfamiliar code.

rules.name: 结束括号后需留空行
rules.description: 在C#代码中，结束括号后未跟随空行会导致规则违规。为了提高代码可读性，应在结束括号后插入空行。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a closing brace is not followed by a blank line in C# code. To enhance readability, a blank line should follow closing braces.

rules.name: 元素文档头注释必须被空行分隔
rules.description: 元素文档头注释没有被空行分隔，影响代码可读性和一致性。
rules.description_en: An element documentation header is not preceded by a blank line, affecting code readability and consistency.

rules.name: 单行注释前须有空行
rules.description: 为促进代码可读性，StyleCop要求在某些情况下的单行注释前需要一个空行，而其他情况下禁止使用空行。这种方式可以提升代码的一致性和可读性。
rules.description_en: To improve code readability, StyleCop requires blank lines before single-line comments in certain situations, while prohibiting them in others. This approach enhances consistency and readability in the code.

rules.name: 元素间空行要求
rules.description: 相邻的C#元素之间缺少空行。这种规则用于提高代码的可读性和一致性。
rules.description_en: Adjacent C# elements are not separated by a blank line. This rule is used to improve code readability and consistency.

rules.name: 文件开头不应有空行
rules.description: 为了提高代码的布局，StyleCop要求文件开头没有空行。
rules.description_en: To improve the layout of the code, StyleCop requires no blank lines at the start of the files.

rules.name: 文件末尾行结束符规范
rules.description: 为了提升代码的可读性和一致性，StyleCop要求文件末尾的行结束符应与项目的设定一致。
rules.description_en: To improve code readability and consistency, StyleCop requires line endings at the end of files to match the project's settings.

rules.name: 多行子语句需包含大括号
rules.description: 当多行语句的大括号被省略时，会违反该规则。要求在多行的C#语句中，必须包含大括号以提高代码的可读性和可维护性。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the opening and closing braces for a multi-line statement have been omitted. The rule requires braces to be present for multi-line C# statements to enhance readability and maintainability.

rules.name: 使用大括号一致性
rules.description: 在连接的`if`/`else if`/`else`结构中，如果某些子句包含了大括号，而其他子句没有，则会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the opening and closing braces for a chained statement have been included for some clauses but omitted for others.

rules.name: 元素文档化要求
rules.description: 如果元素完全缺少文档头或文档头为空，则违反此规则。在C#中，类、构造函数、委托、枚举、事件、析构函数、索引器、接口、方法、属性、记录和结构体均可以有文档头。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs if an element is completely missing a documentation header, or if the header is empty. In C#, classes, constructors, delegates, enums, events, finalizers, indexers, interfaces, methods, properties, records, and structs can have documentation headers.

rules.name: 部分类型元素必须有文档
rules.description: 在C#中，如果一个部分类型元素完全缺失文档头或文档头为空，则会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs if a partial element in C# is completely missing a documentation header or if the header is empty.

rules.name: 枚举项文档头缺失
rules.description: C#语法提供了通过Xml文档头直接在代码中插入文档的机制。缺少枚举项文档头会导致规则违规。
rules.description_en: C# syntax provides a mechanism for inserting documentation directly into code using XML documentation headers. A violation occurs when enumeration items are missing documentation headers.

rules.name: 元素文档必须包含摘要
rules.description: 此规则要求C#元素的XML文档注释必须包含一个`<summary>`标签。
rules.description_en: This rule requires that the XML header documentation for a C# element must have a `<summary>` tag.

rules.name: 部分元素文档必须包含摘要
rules.description: 当部分元素（带有partial属性的元素）的文档头缺少或包含空的`<summary>`或`<content>`标签时，会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the documentation header for a partial element (an element with the partial attribute) is missing a `<summary>` or `<content>` tag, or contains an empty `<summary>` or `<content>` tag.

rules.name: 元素文档必须包含摘要文本
rules.description: 此规则确保C#代码元素的文档头中的`<summary>`标签不为空。
rules.description_en: This rule ensures that the `<summary>` tag within the documentation header for a C# code element is not empty.

rules.name: 部分元素文档必须有摘要文本
rules.description: 用于部分类元素的文档头中的<summary>或<content>标签不能为空。
rules.description_en: The `<summary>` or `<content>` tag within the documentation header for a partial class element must not be empty.

rules.name: 元素文档不应含有默认摘要
rules.description: C#语法提供了通过XML文档头直接在代码中插入类和元素文档的机制。违反此规则会使代码的<summary>标签仍包含Visual Studio生成的默认文档文本。
rules.description_en: C# syntax provides a mechanism for inserting documentation for classes and elements directly into the code through XML documentation headers. A violation of this rule occurs when the <summary> tag contains the default documentation text generated by Visual Studio.

rules.name: 属性文档必须包含<value>标签
rules.description: C#属性的Xml文档注释缺少<value>标签。
rules.description_en: The Xml header documentation for a C# property does not contain a `<value>` tag.

rules.name: 属性文档必须包含值描述
rules.description: C#属性的XML文档中包含空的`<value>`标记。
rules.description_en: The XML header documentation for a C# property contains an empty `<value>` tag.

rules.name: 元素参数必须记录
rules.description: 此规则要求为C#方法、构造函数、委托或索引器元素中的每个参数提供文档说明。
rules.description_en: This rule requires documentation for each parameter in C# methods, constructors, delegates, or indexers.

rules.name: 元素参数文档必须与元素参数匹配
rules.description: 该规则要求方法、构造函数、委托或索引器元素的参数文档与实际参数匹配，包括顺序和数量。
rules.description_en: This rule requires that the parameter documentation for a method, constructor, delegate, or indexer element matches the actual parameters, including order and number.

rules.name: 元素参数文档必须声明参数名称
rules.description: C#元素的文档头部中的`<param>`标签缺少名称属性或名称属性为空，这是不符合文档标准的。
rules.description_en: A `<param>` tag within a C# element's documentation header is missing a name attribute or has an empty name attribute, which is not compliant with documentation standards.

rules.name: 元素参数文档必须包含文字
rules.description: 如果文档中包含一个空的 `<param>` 标签并且没有提供参数的描述，将违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs if a `<param>` tag within an element's documentation header is empty and does not contain a description of the parameter.

rules.name: 元素返回值需有文档说明
rules.description: C#语法提供了一种通过XML文档注释直接在代码中插入类和元素文档的机制。若元素包含返回值而缺少`<returns>`标签，则会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: C# syntax provides a mechanism for inserting documentation for classes and elements directly into the code through the use of XML documentation headers. A violation of this rule occurs if an element containing a return value is missing a `<returns>` tag.

rules.name: 元素返回值文档必须包含文本
rules.description: 当 C# 元素的文档头中的 `<returns>` 标签为空时，将会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs if an element contains an empty `<returns>` tag.

rules.name: 无返回值的文档不应包含返回标签
rules.description: C#代码元素不会返回值，或返回void，但文档头包含了<returns>标签
rules.description_en: A C# code element does not return a value, or returns void, but the documentation header contains a <returns> tag.

rules.name: 泛型类型参数必须有文档说明
rules.description: 一个或多个泛型类型参数缺少文档描述。
rules.description_en: A generic C# element is missing documentation for one or more of its generic type parameters.

rules.name: 泛型类型参数必须在文档中说明（部分类）
rules.description: 当文档中包含`<summary>`标签时，泛型部分类型元素缺少其泛型类型参数的说明。
rules.description_en: A generic, partial C# element is missing documentation for one or more of its generic type parameters when the documentation contains a `<summary>` tag.

rules.name: 泛型类型参数文档匹配
rules.description: 该规则要求C#元素的XML头文档中的`<typeparam>`标签与元素的泛型类型参数匹配。
rules.description_en: This rule requires that the `<typeparam>` tags within the XML header documentation of a C# element match the generic type parameters on the element.

rules.name: 泛型类型参数文档必须声明参数名称
rules.description: C#的泛型元素的Xml文档注释中的`<typeparam>`标签缺少名称属性或者名称属性为空，引发规则违反。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs if the `<typeparam>` tag within the Xml documentation for a generic C# element is missing a name attribute, or contains an empty name attribute.

rules.name: 泛型类型参数文档的文本校验
rules.description: 如果元素的 XML 文档注释中包含空的 `<typeparam>` 标签，则会出现此规则的违规。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs if the element contains an empty `<typeparam>` tag within its XML documentation comment.

rules.name: 属性摘要文档必须匹配访问器
rules.description: 如果属性的摘要文档与访问器不匹配，则违反此规则。文档应描述属性中公开的访问器类型。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs if a property's summary documentation does not match the accessors within the property. The documentation should describe the types of accessors exposed within the property.

rules.name: 元素文档不得复制粘贴
rules.description: 此规则要求所有XML文档中的文本都是唯一的，以防止拼凑或不准确的文档。
rules.description_en: This rule requires all text within the XML documentation to be unique, preventing stitched or inaccurate documentation.

rules.name: 单行注释不能使用文档风格斜杠
rules.content:
# 规则概述
该规则要求C#代码中的单行注释不应以三个斜杠开头，因为这是为XML文档注释头保留的。

## 规则意义
遵循这一规则有助于保持代码风格的一致性，并避免将普通注释误认为是XML文档注释。

## 错误示例
```csharp
/// 这是一个错误的单行注释，因为它以三个斜杠开头。
```

## 正确示例
```csharp
// 这是一个正确的单行注释，因为它以两个斜杠开头。
```
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
This rule mandates that single-line comments in C# code should not begin with three slashes, as these are reserved for XML documentation headers.

## Rule Meaning
Adhering to this rule helps maintain consistency in code style and prevents confusion between regular comments and XML documentation comments.

## Error Example
```csharp
/// This is an incorrect single-line comment because it starts with three slashes.
```

## Correct Example
```csharp
// This is a correct single-line comment because it starts with two slashes.
```
rules.description: 当代码包含以三个斜杠开头的单行注释时，会出现该规则的违反。三个斜杠开头的注释是为XML文档注释头保留的。单行注释应仅以两个斜杠开头。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the code contains a single-line comment which begins with three slashes. Comments beginning with three slashes are reserved for XML documentation headers. Single-line comments should begin with only two slashes.

rules.name: 文档文本不能为空
rules.description: C#代码元素的XML文档标头中包含空标签时，将触发此规则。应在空标签中添加文档文本以修复此类违规。
rules.description_en: This rule flags when the XML documentation header for a C# code element contains an empty tag. To fix such violations, documentation text should be added within the empty tag.

rules.name: 文档文本末尾必须是句号
rules.description: 在C#代码中，Xml文档的部分未以句号结尾会触发此规则违规。确保所有文档段落末尾都有句号。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a section of the Xml documentation for a C# element does not end with a period. Ensure that all sections of the documentation end with a period.

rules.name: 文件头部必须包含标准头信息
rules.description: 当 C# 源文件缺少文件头时，会发生此规则的违例。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when a C# source file is missing a file header.

rules.name: 文件头必须包含版权信息
rules.description: 此规则用于检测C#文件头中缺少版权标签的信息，从而提示开发人员添加适当的版权声明以保护知识产权。
rules.description_en: This rule detects the absence of a copyright tag in the header of a C# file, prompting developers to add appropriate copyright declarations to protect intellectual property.

rules.name: 文件头部必须包含版权信息
rules.description: 当C#代码文件的头部缺少版权信息时，会出现规则违规。该规则确保文件头部的版权标签中包含必要的版权文字。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the file header at the top of a C# code file is missing copyright text. The rule ensures that the copyright tag in file headers contains the necessary copyright text.

rules.name: 文件头版权文本一致性
rules.description: 此规则确保每个C#文件在其文件头中包含指定的版权文本，以便遵循项目的版权声明规范。
rules.description_en: This rule ensures that each C# file includes the specified copyright text in its file header to adhere to the project's copyright declaration standard.

rules.name: 文件头必须包含文件名
rules.description: 当C#文件的头部缺少文件名标签时，会违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the header at the top of a C# file is missing a file name tag.

rules.name: 文件头文件名一致性验证
rules.description: 在C#文件头中，文件标记需与实际文件名一致。
rules.description_en: The file tag within the file header of a C# code file must match the actual filename.

rules.name: 文件头必须包含摘要
rules.description: 此规则在于确保C#文件的文件头包含有效的摘要标签，如无则视作违反规则。
rules.description_en: This rule is aimed at ensuring that the file header of a C# file contains a valid summary tag. Absence of such is considered a rule violation.

rules.name: 文件头必须包含有效的公司名称
rules.description: 当C#文件顶部的文件头未包含公司标签和公司名称文本时违反此规则。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the file header at the top of a C# file does not contain a company tag with company name text.

rules.name: 文件头公司名称文本匹配
rules.description: 当C#文件的文件头中没有包含项目规定的公司名称文本时，违反了此规则。
rules.description_en: This rule is violated when the file header at the top of a C# file does not contain the company name text specified for the project.

rules.name: 构造函数注释规范
rules.description: 该规则要求C#构造函数的XML文档注释中的summary标签以标准文本开头。
rules.description_en: This rule requires the summary tag within the XML documentation header for a C# constructor to begin with the proper standard text.

rules.name: 析构函数文档总结标准化

rules.description_en: The Xml documentation header for a C# destructor does not contain the appropriate summary text. This rule requires that the summary tag within the documentation header for a destructor must begin with standard text.

rules.name: 文件名与类型名匹配

rules.name: 不要使用占位符元素
rules.description: 当元素文档中包含`<placeholder>`元素时，将会出现该规则违规。应审核并移除占位符元素以确保文档的准确性。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs when the element documentation contains `<placeholder>` elements. Placeholder elements should be reviewed and removed to ensure documentation accuracy.

rules.name: 启用XML文档输出
rules.content:
# 规则概述
SA1652规则要求在项目中启用XML文档输出以确保代码的文档化，从而提高代码的可维护性和可读性。

## 规则意义
启用XML文档输出有助于保持代码库良好的文档化实践。它允许生成详细的API文档，方便其他开发者理解和使用代码。

## 错误示例
没有启用项目的XML文档输出。

## 正确示例
确保在项目属性中启用了XML文档输出。

'''csharp
// 在项目的.csproj文件中添加以下配置：
<PropertyGroup>
  <DocumentationFile>bin\Debug\net6.0\MyProject.xml</DocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
'''
rules.content_en:
# Rule Overview
Rule SA1652 requires enabling XML documentation output in the project to ensure code is well-documented, enhancing maintainability and readability.

## Rule Meaning
Enabling XML documentation output promotes good documentation practices within the codebase. It allows for generating detailed API documentation, facilitating better understanding and usage by other developers.

## Error Example
XML documentation output is not enabled in the project.

## Correct Example
Ensure XML documentation output is enabled in the project properties.

'''csharp
// Add the following configuration to the .csproj file of the project:
<PropertyGroup>
  <DocumentationFile>bin\Debug\net6.0\MyProject.xml</DocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
'''

rules.name: 避免在类成员调用中使用'this.'前缀
rules.description: 当代码包含对本地类或基类的实例成员调用并使用了`this.`前缀时违反了此规则。当方法参数名称与标识符相同时，无需报错。
rules.description_en: A violation of this rule occurs whenever the code contains a call to an instance member of the local class or a base class which is prefixed with `this.`. An exception is made when the name of a method parameter conflicts with identifier after the `this.` prefix.

rules.description_en: This rule is violated when a field name does not begin with an underscore.
